211	> \(c\) **Disclosure Statement Approval Milestone.** The Bankruptcy Court shall have entered an order approving the Disclosure Statement as containing adequate information no later than ninety (90) calendar days after the Petition Date.
212	>
213	> \(d\) **Confirmation Milestone.** The Bankruptcy Court shall have entered the Confirmation Order confirming the Plan no later than one hundred thirty-five (135) calendar days after the Petition Date.
214	>
215	> \(e\) **Effective Date Milestone.** The Effective Date of the Plan shall have occurred no later than one hundred sixty-five (165) calendar days after the Petition Date.
216	>
217	> \(f\) **DIP Approval Milestone.** The Bankruptcy Court shall have entered an interim order approving the DIP Facility no later than three (3) Business Days after the Petition Date, and a final order approving the DIP Facility no later than forty-five (45) calendar days after the Petition Date.
218	
219	Any Milestone set forth above may be extended by mutual written agreement of the Company and the Required Consenting Lenders. No such extension shall require the consent of any individual Consenting Lender unless such extension would disproportionately and adversely affect such Consenting Lender.
220	
221	Failure to meet any Milestone shall constitute a potential termination event under Section 6.02(c); *provided, however*, that such failure shall be subject to the cure period set forth in Section 6.02(c) (i.e., ten (10) Business Days from receipt of written notice thereof).
222	
223	**[SECTION 5 --- ADDITIONAL COMPANY COVENANTS]{.underline}**
224	
225	**Section 5.01 --- Information Rights**
226	
227	During the term of this Agreement, the Company shall provide the following information to the Consenting Lenders\' professionals (Sternwick & Calloway LLP and Clearbridge Advisory Group LLC), in each case subject to existing confidentiality agreements and applicable law, including applicable securities laws:
228	
229	> \(a\) monthly unaudited consolidated financial statements of the Company Parties (including a balance sheet, income statement, and statement of cash flows) within thirty (30) days following the end of each calendar month;
230	>
231	> \(b\) weekly 13-week cash flow forecasts, updated and delivered no later than the close of business each Friday (or, if Friday is not a Business Day, the immediately preceding Business Day);
232	>
233	> \(c\) prompt written notice (and in any event within three (3) Business Days) of any event that has resulted in, or would reasonably be expected to result in, a material adverse change in the business, operations, assets, liabilities, or financial condition of the Company Parties, taken as a whole; and
234	>
235	> \(d\) reasonable access to management of the Company Parties for due diligence discussions and meetings, upon reasonable prior notice and during normal business hours.
236	
237	All information delivered pursuant to this Section 5.01 shall be subject to the terms of any applicable confidentiality agreements between the Parties and their respective advisors.
238	
239	**Section 5.02 --- Exclusivity**
240	
241	During the term of this Agreement, the Company shall not (and shall cause its subsidiaries, officers, directors, employees, agents, and advisors not to) directly or indirectly solicit, initiate, encourage, facilitate, or engage in discussions or negotiations with any third party regarding an Alternative Transaction (as defined in Section 7(b)), except as expressly permitted under Section 7 of this Agreement. Any information provided by the Company to a third party regarding a potential transaction involving the Company during the term of this Agreement shall be subject to a confidentiality agreement no less restrictive than the confidentiality agreements in effect between the Parties.
242	
243	**Section 5.03 --- Ordinary Course Operations**
244	
245	The Company Parties shall continue to operate their businesses in the ordinary course, consistent with past practice. Without the prior written consent of the Required Consenting Lenders, the Company shall not:
246	
247	> \(a\) enter into any transaction or series of related transactions with a value in excess of \$10,000,000 outside the ordinary course of business;
248	>
249	> \(b\) incur indebtedness in excess of \$5,000,000 in the aggregate (other than ordinary-course trade payables and obligations under the ABL Facility and existing credit facilities);
250	>
251	> \(c\) sell, transfer, or otherwise dispose of material assets outside the ordinary course of business; or
252	>
253	> \(d\) declare, make, or pay any dividend or distribution to holders of equity interests of the Company.
254	
255	The foregoing consent rights shall be without prejudice to any additional consent rights that may be established in the DIP Credit Agreement or cash collateral orders entered by the Bankruptcy Court.
256	
257	**[SECTION 6 --- TERMINATION]{.underline}**
258	
259	**Section 6.01 --- Termination by the Company**
260	
261	The Company may terminate this Agreement, upon written notice to the Consenting Lenders and their counsel, upon the occurrence of any of the following:
262	
263	> \(a\) a material breach by any Consenting Lender of any representation, warranty, or covenant contained in this Agreement that (if curable) remains uncured for a period of ten (10) Business Days after written notice of such breach is delivered to the breaching Consenting Lender;
264	>
265	> \(b\) the entry of an order by the Bankruptcy Court or any other court of competent jurisdiction (i) converting any of the Chapter 11 Cases to a case under chapter 7 of the Bankruptcy Code, (ii) appointing a chapter 11 trustee or examiner with expanded powers beyond those set forth in section 1106(a)(3) and (4) of the Bankruptcy Code in any of the Chapter 11 Cases, or (iii) dismissing any of the Chapter 11 Cases;
266	>
267	> \(c\) the board of directors of the Company (or any committee thereof) determines, in good faith, after consultation with outside legal counsel, that continued performance under this Agreement would be inconsistent with the exercise of its fiduciary duties under applicable law, subject to the requirements of Section 7(a) (the \"**Fiduciary Out**\"); or
268	>
269	> \(d\) the Required Consenting Lenders have materially breached their respective funding obligations with respect to the DIP Facility, and such breach has not been cured within five (5) Business Days following written notice thereof.
270	
271	**Section 6.02 --- Termination by the Required Consenting Lenders**
272	
273	The Required Consenting Lenders may terminate this Agreement, upon written notice to the Company and its counsel, upon the occurrence of any of the following:
274	
275	> \(a\) a material breach by any Company Party of any representation, warranty, or covenant contained in this Agreement that (if curable) remains uncured for a period of ten (10) Business Days after written notice of such breach is delivered to the Company;
276	>
277	> \(b\) the entry of an order by the Bankruptcy Court or any other court of competent jurisdiction (i) converting any of the Chapter 11 Cases to a case under chapter 7 of the Bankruptcy Code, (ii) appointing a chapter 11 trustee or examiner with expanded powers beyond those set forth in section 1106(a)(3) and (4) of the Bankruptcy Code in any of the Chapter 11 Cases, or (iii) dismissing any of the Chapter 11 Cases;
278	>
279	> \(c\) failure to achieve any Milestone set forth in Section 4 within the time period specified therein, subject to a cure period of ten (10) Business Days following written notice of such failure delivered to the Company;
280	>
281	> \(d\) the Company exercises the Fiduciary Out under Section 7(a);
282	>
283	> \(e\) the entry of an order by the Bankruptcy Court approving any Alternative Transaction;
284	>
285	> \(f\) failure to obtain Bankruptcy Court approval of the DIP Facility (whether interim or final) within the time periods set forth in Section 4(f); or
286	>
287	> \(g\) the entry of an order by the Bankruptcy Court granting relief from the automatic stay to any party with respect to assets of the Company Parties having an aggregate value in excess of \$25,000,000.
288	
289	**Section 6.03 --- Mutual Termination**
290	
291	This Agreement may be terminated at any time by mutual written consent of the Company and the Required Consenting Lenders, without further action by or notice to any other Party.
292	
293	**Section 6.04 --- Effect of Termination**
294	
295	Upon the termination of this Agreement in accordance with this Section 6:
296	
297	> \(a\) all obligations of the Parties under this Agreement shall cease and be of no further force or effect, except for those provisions that expressly survive termination as set forth in clause (c) below;
298	>
299	> \(b\) no Party shall have any liability to any other Party hereunder, except with respect to any willful or intentional breach of this Agreement occurring prior to the date of termination;
300	>
301	> \(c\) the following provisions shall survive termination of this Agreement: this Section 6.04, Section 12 (Fees and Expenses), Section 13 (Governing Law; Dispute Resolution), and Section 14 (Miscellaneous);
302	>
303	> \(d\) any vote cast by a Consenting Lender in favor of the Plan prior to such termination may, at the option of such Consenting Lender, be withdrawn, revoked, and deemed void *ab initio* by delivering written notice of such revocation to the Company and the Bankruptcy Court within five (5) Business Days following the date of termination; and
304	>
305	> \(e\) nothing in this Agreement shall be construed as a waiver of any rights, claims, or causes of action of any Party under the Bankruptcy Code, applicable nonbankruptcy law, or any other agreement, instrument, or document.
306	
307	**[SECTION 7 --- FIDUCIARY OUT; ALTERNATIVE TRANSACTIONS]{.underline}**
308	
309	**Section 7(a) --- Fiduciary Out**
310	
311	Notwithstanding anything to the contrary contained in this Agreement, the board of directors of the Company (or any duly authorized committee thereof) may terminate this Agreement, and the Company Parties shall thereupon be relieved of their obligations hereunder, at any time after the RSA Effective Date if the board of directors (or such committee) determines, in good faith and after consultation with outside legal counsel (Ashford Pierce LLP or such other counsel as may then be retained by the Company), that continued performance by the Company Parties under this Agreement would be inconsistent with the exercise of its fiduciary duties under applicable law; *provided, however*, that the Company shall provide the Consenting Lenders (with copies to Sternwick & Calloway LLP) with at least five (5) Business Days\' prior written notice of its intention to exercise the Fiduciary Out.
312	
313	Such notice shall state that the board of directors has determined to exercise the Fiduciary Out and shall describe the general basis for such determination, but shall not require disclosure of the specific terms of any alternative proposal, transaction, or indication of interest that may have given rise to or informed the board\'s fiduciary determination. For the avoidance of doubt, the exercise of the Fiduciary Out in accordance with this Section 7(a) shall not give rise to any liability of the Company Parties to the Consenting Lenders, except as otherwise provided in Section 6.04.
314	
315	**Section 7(b) --- Alternative Transactions**
316	
317	\(i\) As used herein, \"**Alternative Transaction**\" means any restructuring, dissolution, winding up, liquidation, reorganization, assignment for the benefit of creditors, merger, transaction, consolidation, business combination, joint venture, partnership, sale of all or substantially all assets, financing (other than the DIP Facility), or other transaction involving any Company Party that is an alternative to the Restructuring contemplated by this Agreement and the Restructuring Term Sheet.
318	
319	\(ii\) The Company may pursue an Alternative Transaction if, and only if, the board of directors of the Company determines, in good faith, after consultation with the Company\'s financial advisor (Pendleton Hargrave & Co.) and legal counsel, that such Alternative Transaction would provide a materially better recovery to the Company\'s stakeholders, taken as a whole, than the Restructuring contemplated by this Agreement and the Restructuring Term Sheet.
320	
321	\(iii\) Prior to consummating any Alternative Transaction, the Company shall provide written notice to the Required Consenting Lenders (with copies to Sternwick & Calloway LLP) describing the material terms of the Alternative Transaction in reasonable detail. The Required Consenting Lenders shall have ten (10) Business Days following receipt of such notice (the \"**Matching Period**\") to propose modifications to the terms of the Restructuring that would provide, in the good-faith judgment of the Required Consenting Lenders, comparable or better recovery to the Company\'s stakeholders taken as a whole.
322	
323	\(iv\) If, during the Matching Period, the Required Consenting Lenders propose modifications to the Restructuring that, in the good-faith determination of the board of directors of the Company (after consultation with its financial advisor and legal counsel), would provide comparable or better recovery to the Company\'s stakeholders than the Alternative Transaction, the Company shall continue to perform its obligations under this Agreement as so modified, and the Restructuring Term Sheet shall be deemed amended to reflect such modifications.
324	
325	**[SECTION 8 --- TRANSFER RESTRICTIONS]{.underline}**
326	
327	**Section 8.01 --- General Transfer Restriction.** No Consenting Lender shall sell, assign, transfer, pledge, hypothecate, participate, donate, or otherwise dispose of (including by operation of law) (each, a \"**Transfer**\") any First Lien Term Loan Claim, or any option thereon or any right or interest therein, except in compliance with this Section 8. Any purported Transfer in violation of this Section 8 shall be void *ab initio* and of no force or effect.
328	
329	**Section 8.02 --- Permitted Transfers.** A Consenting Lender may Transfer its First Lien Term Loan Claims solely to:
330	
331	> \(a\) another Consenting Lender (or an affiliate thereof that is a Consenting Lender), without restriction; or
332	>
333	> \(b\) a Qualified Transferee, *provided* that such Qualified Transferee executes and delivers to the Company (with a copy to Sternwick & Calloway LLP and Ashford Pierce LLP) a Joinder Agreement substantially in the form of Exhibit C hereto within five (5) Business Days of the date of such Transfer, pursuant to which the Qualified Transferee shall agree to be bound by all terms of this Agreement as a Consenting Lender with respect to all First Lien Term Loan Claims so acquired.
334	
335	**Section 8.03 --- No Transfers to Non-Consenting Parties.** No Consenting Lender shall Transfer any First Lien Term Loan Claim to any Person that is not a Consenting Lender or a Qualified Transferee that has agreed to become a Consenting Lender and execute a Joinder Agreement in accordance with Section 8.02(b).
336	
337	**Section 8.04 --- Effect of Prohibited Transfer.** Any Transfer made in violation of this Section 8 shall be void *ab initio*, and the Company and the other Consenting Lenders shall have the right to enforce the provisions of this Section 8 through specific performance and injunctive relief.
338	
339	**Section 8.05 --- Qualified Transferee.** A \"**Qualified Transferee**\" is any entity that (a) is an \"eligible assignee\" or \"eligible lender\" (or comparable defined term) under the First Lien Term Loan Credit Agreement, and (b) is not a direct competitor of the Company or an affiliate of a direct competitor of the Company.
340	
341	**[SECTION 9 --- RELEASES]{.underline}**
342	
343	**Section 9.01 --- Mutual Releases.** Effective as of the Effective Date, and to the fullest extent permitted by applicable law: (a) the Company Parties and their estates shall be deemed to have conclusively, absolutely, unconditionally, irrevocably, and forever released, waived, and discharged the Consenting Lenders and their respective current and former officers, directors, managers, members, partners, employees, agents, attorneys (including Sternwick & Calloway LLP), financial advisors (including Clearbridge Advisory Group LLC), and other professionals, in each case solely in their capacities as such, from any and all claims, obligations, rights, suits, damages, causes of action, remedies, and liabilities arising on or prior to the Effective Date; and (b) each Consenting Lender shall be deemed to have conclusively, absolutely, unconditionally, irrevocably, and forever released, waived, and discharged the Company Parties and their respective current and former officers, directors (including Margaret T. Holloway, David R. Nakamura, and Susan K. Pratt), employees, agents, attorneys (including Ashford Pierce LLP and Greystone Whitaker LLP), financial advisors (including Pendleton Hargrave & Co.), and other professionals, in each case solely in their capacities as such, from any and all claims, obligations, rights, suits, damages, causes of action, remedies, and liabilities arising on or prior to the Effective Date.
344	
345	**Section 9.02 --- Scope of Releases.** The releases set forth in Section 9.01 are mutual releases solely among the Parties to this Agreement and their related persons as described therein. Nothing in this Section 9 shall operate or be construed to release, waive, or discharge any claims or causes of action held by or against any Person that is not a Party to this Agreement.
346	
347	**Section 9.03 --- Excluded Claims.** Notwithstanding anything to the contrary in this Section 9, the releases set forth in Section 9.01 shall not apply to (a) any claims arising from willful misconduct, actual fraud, or gross negligence, in each case as determined by a final, non-appealable order of a court of competent jurisdiction; or (b) any obligations arising under this Agreement, the Plan, or any document delivered in connection with the Restructuring that, by their express terms, survive the Effective Date.
348	
349	**Section 9.04 --- Plan Releases.** The Plan shall contain release provisions consistent with, and no broader than, the releases set forth in this Section 9.
350	
351	**[SECTION 10 --- REPRESENTATIONS AND WARRANTIES]{.underline}**
352	
353	**Section 10.01 --- Representations and Warranties of the Company Parties**
354	
355	Each Company Party represents and warrants, severally and not jointly, as of the date hereof and as of the RSA Effective Date:
356	
357	> \(a\) **Organization and Good Standing.** It is duly organized, validly existing, and in good standing under the laws of its jurisdiction of organization and has all requisite corporate, limited liability company, or other organizational power and authority to own its assets and conduct its business as presently conducted.
358	>
359	> \(b\) **Authorization.** It has all requisite corporate or other organizational power and authority to execute, deliver, and perform this Agreement. The execution, delivery, and performance of this Agreement have been duly authorized by all necessary corporate, limited liability company, or other organizational action, including approval by the board of directors (or equivalent governing body) of such Company Party.
360	>
361	> \(c\) **No Conflicts.** The execution, delivery, and performance of this Agreement does not and will not (i) violate any provision of its organizational documents, (ii) conflict with, result in a breach of, or constitute a default under any material agreement to which it is a party (subject to the requirement to obtain Bankruptcy Court approval for certain transactions contemplated herein), or (iii) violate any applicable law, rule, regulation, order, judgment, or decree.
362	>
363	> \(d\) **Enforceability.** This Agreement constitutes a legal, valid, and binding obligation, enforceable against such Company Party in accordance with its terms, subject to applicable bankruptcy, insolvency, fraudulent conveyance, reorganization, moratorium, and similar laws affecting creditors\' rights generally and subject to general equitable principles.
364	>
365	> \(e\) **Financial Information.** The financial information provided to the Consenting Lenders and their advisors is, to the knowledge of such Company Party, accurate and complete in all material respects as of the date provided and does not contain any untrue statement of a material fact or omit to state a material fact necessary to make the statements therein, in light of the circumstances under which they were made, not materially misleading.
366	>
367	> \(f\) **No Material Litigation.** Except as disclosed in writing to the Ad Hoc Group and its counsel, there is no pending or, to the knowledge of such Company Party, threatened action, suit, or proceeding that would reasonably be expected to have a material adverse effect on the ability of the Company Parties to consummate the Restructuring.
368	>
369	> \(g\) **Capital Structure.** The outstanding funded indebtedness of the Company Parties is as set forth in the Recitals.
370	
371	**Section 10.02 --- Representations and Warranties of the Consenting Lenders**
372	
373	Each Consenting Lender severally (and not jointly) represents and warrants as of the date hereof:
374	
375	> \(a\) **Organization and Good Standing.** It is duly organized, validly existing, and in good standing under the laws of its jurisdiction of organization.
376	>
377	> \(b\) **Authorization.** It has all requisite power and authority to execute, deliver, and perform this Agreement, and such execution, delivery, and performance have been duly authorized by all necessary action.
378	>
379	> \(c\) **Holdings.** As of the date hereof, it is the beneficial owner of, or investment advisor or manager with discretionary authority over, the principal amount of First Lien Term Loan Claims set forth on its signature page hereto, free and clear of any liens, claims, or encumbrances that would impair its ability to perform its obligations hereunder.
380	>
381	> \(d\) **No Conflicts.** The execution, delivery, and performance of this Agreement does not violate any applicable law or its organizational documents or any material agreement to which it is a party.
382	>
383	> \(e\) **Enforceability.** This Agreement constitutes a legal, valid, and binding obligation, enforceable against such Consenting Lender in accordance with its terms, subject to applicable bankruptcy, insolvency, and similar laws.
384	>
385	> \(f\) **Sophistication.** It is an \"accredited investor\" (as defined in Rule 501 of Regulation D under the Securities Act of 1933) or a \"qualified institutional buyer\" (as defined in Rule 144A under the Securities Act of 1933).
386	
387	**[SECTION 11 --- GOVERNANCE OF THE REORGANIZED COMPANY]{.underline}**
388	
389	**Section 11.01 --- Board Composition.** The board of directors of the Reorganized Company shall be determined and disclosed in the Plan Supplement no later than ten (10) calendar days prior to the Confirmation Hearing. The composition of the initial board of the Reorganized Company shall be determined by the Company in consultation with the Required Consenting Lenders. The initial board shall consist of a number of directors to be set forth in the Plan Supplement, and each director shall serve in accordance with the organizational documents of the Reorganized Company.
390	
391	**Section 11.02 --- Management.** Current senior management of the Company, including Margaret T. Holloway (Chief Executive Officer), David R. Nakamura (Chief Financial Officer), and Susan K. Pratt (General Counsel), shall continue in their respective current roles through the Effective Date. On or promptly following the Effective Date, the Reorganized Company shall offer such officers new employment agreements on terms to be negotiated in good faith among the Reorganized Company\'s board of directors and such officers.
392	
393	**Section 11.03 --- Management Incentive Plan.** On or promptly following the Effective Date, the Reorganized Company shall adopt the Management Incentive Plan, reserving up to 10% of Pro Forma Equity (on a fully diluted basis) for management and key employees of the Reorganized Company. The MIP shall provide that 50% of the equity reserved thereunder shall vest on the Effective Date and 50% shall be subject to time-based vesting in equal annual installments over a period of three (3) years following the Effective Date. Specific terms, conditions, individual allocations, and the form of equity-based awards shall be determined by the board of directors of the Reorganized Company in consultation with the Required Consenting Lenders.
394	
395	**[SECTION 12 --- FEES AND EXPENSES]{.underline}**
396	
397	**Section 12.01 --- Ad Hoc Group Professionals.** The Company shall pay the reasonable and documented fees and expenses of (a) Sternwick & Calloway LLP, as legal counsel to the Ad Hoc Group, and (b) Clearbridge Advisory Group LLC, as financial advisor to the Ad Hoc Group, in each case in accordance with the terms of their respective engagement letters. Fees and expenses incurred prepetition shall be paid without the requirement of Bankruptcy Court approval; fees and expenses incurred postpetition shall be paid subject to Bankruptcy Court approval. Invoices shall be submitted to the Company on a monthly basis (or more frequently as reasonably determined by such professional) and shall be paid within ten (10) Business Days of receipt, subject to the Company\'s reasonable right to object to specific time entries or disbursements.
398	
399	**Section 12.02 --- Company Professionals.** For the avoidance of doubt, the Company\'s professionals, including Ashford Pierce LLP (restructuring counsel), Greystone Whitaker LLP (proposed conflicts counsel), Pendleton Hargrave & Co. (financial advisor and investment banker), and Hartfield & Dunn CPAs (auditing firm), shall be compensated in accordance with their respective engagement letters and, to the extent incurred postpetition, subject to Bankruptcy Court approval pursuant to applicable provisions of the Bankruptcy Code.
400	
401	**Section 12.03 --- Professional Fee Carveout.** The Professional Fee Carveout shall be in the aggregate amount of \$22,500,000, allocated as set forth in Section 1 hereof (\$15,000,000 for professionals retained by the Company Parties and \$7,500,000 for professionals retained by any official committee of unsecured creditors). The Professional Fee Carveout shall be a condition to the entry of any order approving the DIP Facility and shall not be subject to reduction.
402	
403	**[SECTION 13 --- GOVERNING LAW; DISPUTE RESOLUTION]{.underline}**
404	
405	**Section 13.01 --- Governing Law.** This Agreement shall be governed by and construed in accordance with the internal laws of the State of New York, without giving effect to any choice-of-law or conflict-of-law rules or provisions (whether of the State of New York or any other jurisdiction) that would cause the application of the laws of any jurisdiction other than the State of New York.
406	
407	**Section 13.02 --- Jurisdiction.** Prior to the Petition Date, each Party irrevocably and unconditionally submits to the exclusive jurisdiction of the United States District Court for the Southern District of New York or, if such court lacks subject matter jurisdiction, the courts of the State of New York located in the Borough of Manhattan, City of New York, for the purposes of any action, suit, or proceeding arising out of or relating to this Agreement. Following the Petition Date, all disputes arising under or in connection with this Agreement shall be resolved exclusively by the Bankruptcy Court, and each Party irrevocably consents to the jurisdiction of the Bankruptcy Court for such purpose.
408	
409	**Section 13.03 --- Waiver of Jury Trial.** EACH PARTY HEREBY IRREVOCABLY WAIVES, TO THE FULLEST EXTENT PERMITTED BY APPLICABLE LAW, ANY RIGHT IT MAY HAVE TO A TRIAL BY JURY IN ANY LEGAL PROCEEDING DIRECTLY OR INDIRECTLY ARISING OUT OF OR RELATING TO THIS AGREEMENT OR THE TRANSACTIONS CONTEMPLATED HEREBY.
410	
411	**[SECTION 14 --- MISCELLANEOUS]{.underline}**
412	
413	**Section 14.01 --- Notices.** All notices, requests, demands, and other communications under this Agreement shall be in writing and shall be deemed to have been duly given or made (a) when delivered in person, (b) when sent by email (with confirmation of receipt), or (c) one (1) Business Day after deposit with a nationally recognized overnight courier service, in each case to the following addresses (or such other address as may be specified by written notice):
414	
415	> If to the Company:
416	>
417	> Ridgeline Hospitality Group, Inc. 900 Lakeshore Boulevard, Suite 2400 Chicago, IL 60611
418	>
419	> Attention: Susan K. Pratt, General Counsel
420	>
421	> Email: spratt@ridgelinehospitality.com
422	>
423	> with a copy (which shall not constitute notice) to:
424	>
425	> Ashford Pierce LLP 1261 Avenue of the Americas, 38th Floor New York, NY 10020
426	>
427	> Attention: Claire E. Vasquez
428	>
429	> Email: cvasquez@ashfordpierce.com
430	>
431	> If to a Consenting Lender, to the address set forth on such Consenting Lender\'s signature page hereto, with a copy (which shall not constitute notice) to:
432	>
433	> Sternwick & Calloway LLP 595 Madison Avenue, 30th Floor New York, NY 10022
434	>
435	> Attention: Jonathan M. Garvey
436	>
437	> Email: jgarvey@sternwickcalloway.com
438	
439	**Section 14.02 --- Entire Agreement.** This Agreement (including the Restructuring Term Sheet, the DIP Term Sheet, and all Exhibits and Schedules hereto) constitutes the entire agreement among the Parties with respect to the subject matter hereof and supersedes all prior and contemporaneous negotiations, agreements, representations, warranties, and understandings, whether written or oral, with respect to such subject matter.
440	
441	**Section 14.03 --- Amendments and Waivers.** No provision of this Agreement may be amended, modified, waived, or supplemented except by a written instrument signed by the Company and the Required Consenting Lenders; *provided, however*, that (a) any amendment that adversely affects the economic treatment of any individual Consenting Lender in a manner disproportionate to other Consenting Lenders shall require the prior written consent of such affected Consenting Lender; and (b) any amendment to the Milestones set forth in Section 4 shall require the consent of the Required Consenting Lenders.
442	
443	**Section 14.04 --- No Third-Party Beneficiaries.** This Agreement is solely for the benefit of the Parties hereto and their respective permitted successors and assigns. Nothing in this Agreement, express or implied, shall create or confer upon any Person that is not a Party hereto (including any holder of Second Lien Notes, Senior Unsecured Notes, or any official committee appointed in the Chapter 11 Cases) any rights, benefits, remedies, or obligations of any nature whatsoever.
444	
445	**Section 14.05 --- Severability.** If any provision of this Agreement is held to be illegal, invalid, or unenforceable under present or future laws, such provision shall be fully severable, and this Agreement shall be construed and enforced as if such illegal, invalid, or unenforceable provision had never comprised a part of this Agreement, and the remaining provisions of this Agreement shall remain in full force and effect.
446	
447	**Section 14.06 --- Headings.** The headings of the sections, subsections, and paragraphs of this Agreement are inserted for convenience of reference only and shall not affect the interpretation or construction hereof.
448	
449	**Section 14.07 --- Counterparts.** This Agreement may be executed in one or more counterparts, each of which shall be deemed an original and all of which together shall constitute one and the same instrument. Delivery of an executed counterpart by electronic mail in .pdf format or by electronic signature (including DocuSign or similar platforms) shall be equally effective as delivery of an original executed counterpart.
450

**Section 14.08 --- Specific Performance.** The Parties acknowledge and agree that irreparable damage would occur if any provision of this Agreement were not performed in accordance with its specific terms or were otherwise breached. Accordingly, each Party shall be entitled to seek specific performance and injunctive or other equitable relief as a remedy for any breach or threatened breach of this Agreement, without the necessity of proving actual damages or posting any bond or other security.

**Section 14.09 --- Reservation of Rights.** Except as expressly provided in this Agreement, nothing herein is intended to, or does, in any manner waive, limit, impair, or restrict the ability of any Party to protect and preserve its rights, remedies, and interests, including any claims against any other Party. If this Agreement is terminated in accordance with its terms, the Parties reserve all of their respective rights, remedies, claims, and defenses.

**Section 14.10 --- Relationship Among Parties.** No Party shall be deemed to be a partner, joint venturer, co-owner, or fiduciary of any other Party solely by reason of this Agreement. The Parties acknowledge that the Consenting Lenders are not acting as a \"group\" for purposes of Section 13(d) of the Securities Exchange Act of 1934, as amended, and nothing in this Agreement shall be construed as creating such a group.

**Section 14.11 --- Acknowledgments.** Each Party acknowledges that (a) it has had the opportunity to be represented by counsel in connection with this Agreement and the transactions contemplated hereby; (b) this Agreement was negotiated at arm\'s length among the Parties with the benefit of legal and financial advisors; (c) no Party is relying on any statement, representation, or warranty not expressly set forth in this Agreement; and (d) each Party has had the opportunity to review and negotiate the terms of this Agreement and has voluntarily agreed to the same.

*\[Remainder of page intentionally left blank; signature pages follow.\]*

**IN WITNESS WHEREOF**, the Parties have caused this Restructuring Support Agreement to be executed and delivered as of the date first set forth above.

**COMPANY PARTIES**

**[RESTRUCTURING TERM SHEET]{.underline}**

This Restructuring Term Sheet (this \"Term Sheet\") is attached as Exhibit A to the Restructuring Support Agreement dated \[●\], 2025 (the \"RSA\"), among Ridgeline Hospitality Group, Inc., its subsidiaries, and the Consenting Lenders party thereto. Capitalized terms used but not defined herein shall have the meanings ascribed to them in the RSA. This Term Sheet is subject in all respects to the definitive documents implementing the Restructuring and does not constitute a binding commitment or obligation except to the extent set forth in the RSA.

**I. Overview of the Restructuring**

Ridgeline Hospitality Group, Inc. and its direct and indirect subsidiaries (the \"Company Parties\") will pursue a prepackaged chapter 11 restructuring in the United States Bankruptcy Court for the District of Delaware. The Plan will provide for: (a) deleveraging the Company\'s balance sheet from approximately \$1.95 billion in total funded debt; (b) providing the Company with new DIP financing during the Chapter 11 Cases and exit financing upon emergence; (c) equitizing a portion of the first lien term loan debt; and (d) distributing equity and other consideration to stakeholders as set forth below.

**II. Treatment of Claims and Interests**

**A. ABL Revolving Credit Facility Claims (Unimpaired).** Holders of claims under the ABL Facility (approximately \$80,000,000 drawn as of the Petition Date) shall be paid in full in cash on the Effective Date or, at the election of the ABL Agent (Briarwood Commercial Bank, N.A.) and with the consent of the Required Consenting Lenders, shall receive replacement obligations under a new ABL revolving credit facility on market terms. ABL Claims are unimpaired and are not entitled to vote on the Plan.

**B. First Lien Term Loan Claims (Impaired --- Entitled to Vote).** Each holder of allowed First Lien Term Loan Claims (approximately \$1,190,000,000 outstanding) shall receive its *pro rata* share of:

> \(a\) **New Exit First Lien Term Loans** in the aggregate principal amount of \$595,000,000, representing approximately 50% of the outstanding face amount of the First Lien Term Loan (\$1,190,000,000 x 50% = \$595,000,000), on terms to be set forth in the Exit Facility credit documentation; and
>
> \(b\) **72% of the Pro Forma Equity** in the Reorganized Company, subject to dilution by the Management Incentive Plan (up to 10%).

First Lien Term Loan Claims are impaired. This class is entitled to vote on the Plan.

**C. Second Lien Secured Notes Claims (Impaired --- Entitled to Vote).** Each holder of allowed Second Lien Notes Claims (approximately \$380,000,000 outstanding, 9.75% fixed rate, due March 15, 2026; indenture trustee: Commonwealth National Trust Company) shall receive its *pro rata* share of **12% of the Pro Forma Equity** in the Reorganized Company, subject to dilution by the MIP. Second Lien Notes Claims are impaired. This class is entitled to vote on the Plan. The ad hoc group of second lien holders is represented by Kelton Harris & Roe LLP and is not currently a party to the RSA.

**D. Senior Unsecured Notes Claims (Impaired --- Entitled to Vote).** Each holder of allowed Senior Unsecured Notes Claims (approximately \$300,000,000 outstanding, 7.50% fixed rate, due September 15, 2025; indenture trustee: Atlas Fiduciary Services, Inc.) shall receive its *pro rata* share of:

> \(a\) **6% of the Pro Forma Equity** in the Reorganized Company, subject to dilution by the MIP; and
>
> \(b\) **Warrants** for an additional 3% of the Pro Forma Equity, with a strike price based on a total enterprise value of \$1,300,000,000.

Senior Unsecured Notes Claims are impaired. This class is entitled to vote on the Plan.

**E. General Unsecured Claims (Unimpaired).** Holders of allowed general unsecured claims (trade claims, vendor claims, and similar obligations) shall be paid in full in the ordinary course of business or otherwise receive treatment rendering such claims unimpaired under section 1124 of the Bankruptcy Code.

**F. Intercompany Claims.** Intercompany claims shall be reinstated, adjusted, contributed, or discharged as determined by the Company with the consent of the Required Consenting Lenders, to the extent necessary to implement the Restructuring.

**G. Existing Equity Interests (Impaired --- Deemed to Reject).** All existing equity interests in Ridgeline Hospitality Group, Inc. shall be cancelled, released, and extinguished on the Effective Date, and holders thereof shall not receive any distribution on account of such interests.

**III. Equity Reconciliation**

  ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
  **Recipient**                  **Equity Allocation**   **Subject to MIP Dilution**
  ------------------------------ ----------------------- -----------------------------
  First Lien Term Loan Holders   72%                     Yes (up to 10%)

  Second Lien Noteholders        12%                     Yes (up to 10%)

  Senior Unsecured Noteholders   6% + 3% warrants        Yes (up to 10%)

  Management Incentive Plan      Up to 10%               N/A

  **Total**                      **100%**                ---
  ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------

**IV. DIP Facility Summary**

> • **Facility Amount:** \$175,000,000 new money
>
> • **DIP Lenders:** Certain members of the Ad Hoc Group
>
> • **Interest Rate:** SOFR + 650 basis points
>
> • **Default Rate:** Additional 200 basis points
>
> • **Fees:** None
>
> • **Maturity:** 6 months from the Petition Date
>
> • **Roll-Up:** \$75,000,000 of prepetition First Lien Term Loan Claims of the DIP Lenders shall be rolled up into the DIP Facility upon entry of the final DIP order (total DIP claims: \$250,000,000)
>
> • **Use of Proceeds:** Working capital, payment of professional fees, and other costs of the Restructuring
>
> • **Security:** Superpriority administrative expense claim (section 364(c)(1)); first-priority priming liens on all assets (section 364(d)); subject to Professional Fee Carveout
>
> • **Budget:** 13-week operating budget, updated bi-weekly; permitted variance: +/- 15% line-item, +/- 10% aggregate on a rolling 4-week tested basis
>
> • **Professional Fee Carveout:** \$22,500,000 (\$15,000,000 debtor; \$7,500,000 committee)

**V. Management Incentive Plan**

> • **Pool Size:** Up to 10% of Pro Forma Equity on a fully diluted basis
>
> • **Vesting:** 50% vesting on the Effective Date; 50% subject to time-based vesting over three (3) years in equal annual installments
>
> • **Participants:** CEO, CFO, General Counsel, and other senior management and key employees as determined by the board of the Reorganized Company
>
> • **Form of Awards:** Restricted stock, stock options, restricted stock units, or such other equity-based instruments as the board determines
>
> • **Terms:** Specific terms, conditions, and individual allocations to be determined by the board of the Reorganized Company in consultation with the Required Consenting Lenders prior to the Effective Date

**VI. Professional Fee Carveout**

The Professional Fee Carveout shall consist of \$22,500,000 in the aggregate, allocated as follows: (a) \$15,000,000 for professionals retained by the Company Parties (including Ashford Pierce LLP, Greystone Whitaker LLP, Pendleton Hargrave & Co., and Hartfield & Dunn CPAs); and (b) \$7,500,000 for professionals retained by any official committee of unsecured creditors. The Professional Fee Carveout shall not be subject to reduction and shall be a condition to entry of any DIP order.

**VII. Releases.** The Plan shall contain mutual releases among the Debtors, the Reorganized Debtors, the Consenting Lenders, and their respective current and former officers, directors, managers, members, employees, agents, attorneys, financial advisors, and other professionals, in each case solely in their capacities as such. Releases shall not cover claims arising from willful misconduct, actual fraud, or gross negligence as determined by a final non-appealable order of a court of competent jurisdiction.

**VIII. Other Plan Terms**

The Plan shall contain customary conditions to the Effective Date, including entry of the Confirmation Order, effectiveness of the Exit Facility, and satisfaction of all conditions under the DIP Credit Agreement. The Plan shall provide for the assumption or rejection of executory contracts and unexpired leases as determined by the Company with the consent of the Required Consenting Lenders. The Plan shall contain customary exculpation provisions for the Debtors, the Reorganized Debtors, and their professionals. The anticipated filing jurisdiction is the United States Bankruptcy Court for the District of Delaware.

24	ARTICLE I — DEFINITIONS

39	"DIP Facility" means the debtor-in-possession credit facility to be provided to the Company Parties on the terms and conditions set forth in the DIP Term Sheet attached hereto as Exhibit B.
40	"Disclosure Statement" means the disclosure statement for the Plan, in form and substance acceptable to the Company and the Required Consenting Lenders.
41	"Effective Date" means the date on which all conditions precedent to the effectiveness of the Plan have been satisfied or waived in accordance with the terms of the Plan and the Confirmation Order.

51	"Management Incentive Plan" or "MIP" means an equity-based management incentive plan providing for the issuance of equity interests in the Reorganized Company representing up to [-ten percent (10%)-] [+seven and one-half percent (7.5%)+] of the Pro Forma Equity Interests, on terms and conditions to be determined by the New Board in consultation with the Required Consenting Lenders.
52	"MIP Vesting Schedule" means the vesting schedule applicable to awards granted under the MIP, providing that [-fifty percent (50%) shall vest on the Effective Date and fifty percent (50%) shall be subject to time-based vesting over a three (3)-year period-] [+twenty-five percent (25%) shall vest on the Effective Date and seventy-five percent (75%) shall be subject to performance-based vesting metrics (as determined by the board of directors of the Reorganized Company in consultation with the Required Consenting Lenders) over a four (4)-year period+].

54	[+"Minimum Liquidity Threshold" means, as of any date of determination, a trailing four (4)-week average of Liquidity of not less than Forty Million Dollars ($40,000,000).+]

59	"Professional Fee Carveout" means the aggregate amount of [-(a) Fifteen Million Dollars ($15,000,000) for professional fees and expenses of retained professionals of the Company Parties (the "Debtor Professional Carveout") and (b) Seven Million Five Hundred Thousand Dollars ($7,500,000) for professional fees and expenses of retained professionals of any statutory committee appointed in the Chapter 11 Cases (the "Committee Professional Carveout"), for an aggregate Professional Fee Carveout of Twenty-Two Million Five Hundred Thousand Dollars ($22,500,000)-] [+(a) Ten Million Dollars ($10,000,000) for professional fees and expenses of retained professionals of the Company Parties (the "Debtor Professional Carveout") and (b) Five Million Dollars ($5,000,000) for professional fees and expenses of retained professionals of any statutory committee appointed in the Chapter 11 Cases (the "Committee Professional Carveout"), for an aggregate Professional Fee Carveout of Fifteen Million Dollars ($15,000,000)+].

62	"Released Parties" has the meaning set forth in Section 10.01.
63	"Reorganized Company" means Reorganized Ridgeline Hospitality Group, Inc., and [+including, without limitation,+] each of its reorganized subsidiaries, in each case, on and after the Effective Date.
64	"Required Consenting Lenders" means Consenting First Lien Lenders holding at least sixty-six and two-thirds percent (66⅔%) of the aggregate principal amount of First Lien Term Loan Claims held by all Consenting First Lien Lenders.
65	"Restructuring Term Sheet" means the term sheet attached hereto as Exhibit A and incorporated herein by reference.
66	"Restructuring Transactions" means the transactions contemplated by this Agreement and the Restructuring Term Sheet.
67	"RSA Effective Date" means the date on which all conditions precedent to the effectiveness of this Agreement have been satisfied or waived, including the execution and delivery of this Agreement by each of the Parties.

73	ARTICLE II — RESTRUCTURING TERM SHEET AND PLAN TERMS
74	Section 2.01. Restructuring Term Sheet. The principal terms of the Restructuring Transactions are set forth in the Restructuring Term Sheet attached hereto as Exhibit A and incorporated herein by reference. [+The Restructuring Term Sheet is an integral part of this Agreement, and all terms set forth therein shall have the same force and effect as if set forth in the body of this Agreement.+] In the event of any conflict between the terms of the body of this Agreement and the Restructuring Term Sheet, the terms of the Restructuring Term Sheet shall control, unless expressly stated otherwise.
75	Section 2.02. Plan of Reorganization. The Company Parties shall file the Plan with the Bankruptcy Court in form and substance [-reasonably acceptable to-] [+acceptable to+] the Company and the Required Consenting Lenders. The Plan shall include, among other things, the treatment of Claims and Interests set forth in Article VI hereof, the release and injunction provisions set forth in Article X hereof, and such other terms as are customary for a prepackaged plan of reorganization of a company of comparable size and complexity.

The Company Parties shall prepare and file the Disclosure Statement with the Bankruptcy Court in form and substance [-reasonably acceptable to-] [+acceptable to+] the Company and the Required Consenting Lenders. 77	Section 2.04. DIP Financing. The Company Parties shall seek approval of the DIP Facility on the terms and conditions set forth in the DIP Term Sheet attached hereto as Exhibit B. [+The Company shall file a motion seeking interim and final approval of the DIP Facility within two (2) Business Days of the Petition Date.+] The DIP Facility shall provide funding necessary to administer the Chapter 11 Cases and operate the Company Parties' businesses during the pendency thereof.
78	[+Section 2.05. Cash Collateral. Notwithstanding any order of the Bankruptcy Court authorizing the use of Cash Collateral, the Company Parties shall not, without the prior written consent of the Required Consenting Lenders, use Cash Collateral in an amount exceeding (a) Two Million Dollars ($2,000,000) in any single transaction or (b) Five Million Dollars ($5,000,000) in the aggregate, in each case outside the ordinary course of business. Any request for consent under this Section 2.05 shall be delivered to counsel for the Ad Hoc Group and shall specify in reasonable detail the proposed use of Cash Collateral. The Required Consenting Lenders shall respond to any such request within three (3) Business Days of receipt thereof.+]
79	ARTICLE III — COMMITMENTS OF THE PARTIES
80	Section 3.01. Commitments of the Company Parties. During the period commencing on the RSA Effective Date and ending on the Termination Date, each Company Party agrees to:
81	(a) support and use [-commercially reasonable efforts-] [+reasonable best efforts+] [+and in consultation with the Required Consenting Lenders+] to consummate and make effective the Restructuring Transactions, including the Plan and all documents and transactions contemplated thereunder;
82	(b) commence the Chapter 11 Cases within the timeframe set forth in Section 4.01(a) and use reasonable best efforts to satisfy each of the Milestones;
83	(c) prepare and file the Plan, the Disclosure Statement, and all related solicitation materials, motions, pleadings, orders, and other documents (collectively, the "Definitive Documents") in form and substance acceptable to the Company and the Required Consenting Lenders;
84	(d) seek approval of the DIP Facility on the terms set forth in the DIP Term Sheet and in accordance with the Milestones;
85	(e) not take any action, or fail to take any action, that is inconsistent in any material respect with this Agreement, the Restructuring Term Sheet, the Plan, or the Restructuring Transactions, or that would delay, impede, or prevent the consummation of the Restructuring Transactions;
86	(f) timely provide all financial information reasonably requested by the Ad Hoc Group and its advisors, [+including, without limitation, weekly cash flow projections and variance reports,+] in each case subject to execution by the applicable recipients of customary non-disclosure agreements;
87	[+(g) support any motion by the Required Consenting Lenders to extend the exclusive periods under section 1121 of the Bankruptcy Code to the maximum extent permitted by applicable law;+]
88	[+(h) promptly upon the RSA Effective Date and continuing until the Petition Date, provide two (2) observers designated by the Required Consenting Lenders (the "Board Observers") with (i) notice of all meetings of the board of directors of the Company (and any committee thereof) not less than two (2) Business Days prior to any such meeting, (ii) copies of all materials provided to the board of directors (and any committee thereof) contemporaneously with delivery to the directors, and (iii) the right to attend (but not vote at) all such meetings, whether in person or by teleconference or videoconference. The Board Observers shall be subject to customary confidentiality obligations; provided, that the Company acknowledges that the Consenting First Lien Lenders may trade in the First Lien Term Loan claims in accordance with applicable securities laws and the Company shall, upon request, establish customary information barrier procedures to facilitate such trading; and+]
89	(i) comply in all material respects with the terms and conditions of this Agreement.
90	Section 3.02. Commitments of the Consenting First Lien Lenders. During the period commencing on the RSA Effective Date and ending on the Termination Date, each Consenting First Lien Lender agrees, severally and not jointly, to:
91	(a) [+timely+] vote (or cause to be voted) all of its First Lien Term Loan Claims in favor of the Plan, and not change, withdraw, or revoke (or cause to be changed, withdrawn, or revoked) such vote;
92	(b) not opt out of any releases provided under the Plan [+in the Chapter 11 Cases+], to the extent applicable to such Consenting First Lien Lender;
93	(c) not direct the First Lien Agent to take any action that is inconsistent with this Agreement, the Plan, or the Restructuring Transactions;
94	(d) support approval of the DIP Facility by the Bankruptcy Court;
95	(e) not Transfer any First Lien Term Loan Claims except in accordance with Article VIII;
96	(f) support approval of the Disclosure Statement by the Bankruptcy Court;
97	(g) not commence or support any alternative plan of reorganization or liquidation, or propose, support, or vote in favor of any Alternative Transaction, in each case, that is inconsistent with the Restructuring Transactions; and
98	(h) comply in all material respects with the terms and conditions of this Agreement.
99	ARTICLE IV — MILESTONES
100	Section 4.01. Milestones. [+Time being of the essence,+] the following milestones (each, a "Milestone" and collectively, the "Milestones") must be satisfied unless waived or extended in accordance with Section 4.02:
101	(a) Filing Milestone. The Company Parties shall commence the Chapter 11 Cases no later than [-five (5)-] [+three (3)+] Business Days after the RSA Effective Date.
102	(b) DIP Approval Milestone. [+The Company Parties shall obtain interim approval of the DIP Facility no later than five (5) Business Days after the Petition Date, and+] the Company Parties shall obtain final approval of the DIP Facility no later than forty-five (45) days after the Petition Date.
103	(c) Disclosure Statement Filing Milestone. The Company Parties shall file the Disclosure Statement and the Plan no later than [-forty-five (45)-] [+thirty (30)+] days after the Petition Date.
104	(d) Disclosure Statement Approval Milestone. The Bankruptcy Court shall have entered an order approving the Disclosure Statement no later than [-ninety (90)-] [+seventy-five (75)+] days after the Petition Date.
105	(e) Confirmation Milestone. The Bankruptcy Court shall have entered the Confirmation Order no later than [-one hundred thirty-five (135)-] [+one hundred ten (110)+] days after the Petition Date.
106	(f) Emergence Milestone. The Effective Date shall have occurred no later than [-one hundred sixty-five (165)-] [+one hundred forty (140)+] days after the Petition Date.
107	Section 4.02. Waiver and Extension of Milestones. Any Milestone may be waived[+,+] [-or extended by the Company with the consent of the Required Consenting Lenders (such consent not to be unreasonably withheld)-] [+extended, or modified only by the written consent of the Required Consenting Lenders in their sole and absolute discretion+]. The Company shall provide prompt written notice to counsel for the Ad Hoc Group upon satisfaction of each Milestone.
108	ARTICLE V — DIP FINANCING TERMS
109	Section 5.01. DIP Facility. The DIP Facility shall be provided on the terms and conditions set forth in the DIP Term Sheet attached hereto as Exhibit B. The key terms of the DIP Facility include the following:
110	(a) Facility Amount: $175,000,000 in aggregate new money commitments.
111	(b) Interest Rate: [-SOFR + 650 basis points-] [+SOFR + 800 basis points+] per annum, with interest payable in cash monthly in arrears.
112	(c) Upfront Fee: [+Three percent (3.00%) of the aggregate commitment amount ($175,000,000 × 3.00% = $5,250,000), payable in cash on the closing date of the DIP Facility.+]
113	(d) Exit Fee: [+Two percent (2.00%) of the aggregate outstanding principal amount of the DIP Facility ($175,000,000 × 2.00% = $3,500,000), payable on the earlier of the Effective Date or the termination of the DIP Credit Agreement.+]
114	(e) Roll-Up: [-$75,000,000-] [+$175,000,000 (i.e., 100%)+] of the DIP Facility commitments shall be rolled up into the Exit Facility on the Effective Date, on a dollar-for-dollar basis, with such rolled-up amounts receiving the same priority, liens, and other protections as the DIP Facility obligations.
115	(f) Maturity: Six (6) months from the Petition Date.
116	(g) DIP Lenders: Certain members of the Ad Hoc Group and their respective designees.

ARTICLE VII — FIDUCIARY OUT; ALTERNATIVE TRANSACTIONS
Section 7.01. Fiduciary Out.
(a) Notwithstanding anything to the contrary in this Agreement, the Company Parties' obligations hereunder may be terminated by the Company if the board of directors of the Company determines, in good faith and upon the written advice of outside legal counsel, that continued performance under this Agreement would be inconsistent with the exercise of its fiduciary duties under applicable law (the "Fiduciary Out").
(b) Prior to exercising the Fiduciary Out, the Company shall provide [-five (5)-] [+ten (10)+] Business Days' prior written notice to [-the Ad Hoc Group-] [+counsel to the Ad Hoc Group (with a copy to counsel to the Required Consenting Lenders)+] of the Company's intention to exercise the Fiduciary Out.
[+(c) Such notice shall include a written description in reasonable detail of (i) the facts and circumstances giving rise to the board's determination, (ii) any Alternative Transaction, proposal, or expression of interest that the board considered in making such determination, including the identity of any counterparty, and (iii) the material terms of any such Alternative Transaction, proposal, or expression of interest.+]
(d) During the [-five (5)-] [+ten (10)+] Business Day notice period, the Company shall negotiate in good faith with the Required Consenting Lenders regarding any modifications to this Agreement or the Restructuring Transactions that would obviate the need to exercise the Fiduciary Out. If, following such good-faith negotiations, the board of directors of the Company still determines that the exercise of the Fiduciary Out is required by its fiduciary duties, the Company may terminate this Agreement by delivering written notice of termination to counsel for the Ad Hoc Group.
Section 7.02. Alternative Transaction.
(a) The Company may not consummate or enter into a binding agreement with respect to an Alternative Transaction unless [-such Alternative Transaction would provide a materially better recovery to stakeholders of the Company than the Restructuring Transactions contemplated hereby-] [+such Alternative Transaction would provide an aggregate recovery to the estate that is at least fifteen percent (15%) greater than the aggregate recovery provided to the estate under the Restructuring Transactions contemplated hereby, as reasonably determined by the Company in consultation with its financial advisor+].
(b) Prior to consummating or entering into a binding agreement with respect to an Alternative Transaction, the Company shall provide the Required Consenting Lenders with [-ten (10)-] [+fifteen (15)+] Business Days to match or improve upon the terms of such Alternative Transaction (the "Matching Period"). [-During the Matching Period, the Company shall negotiate in good faith with the Required Consenting Lenders regarding any revised terms.-] [+During the Matching Period, the Company shall (i) negotiate in good faith with the Required Consenting Lenders regarding any revised terms, (ii) provide the Required Consenting Lenders and their advisors with all information (including non-public information) provided to the counterparty proposing the Alternative Transaction, and (iii) not enter into any exclusivity arrangement with the counterparty to the Alternative Transaction.+] If the Required Consenting Lenders match or improve upon the terms of the Alternative Transaction during the Matching Period, the Company shall not pursue the Alternative Transaction and shall continue to perform its obligations under this Agreement.
ARTICLE VIII — TRANSFER RESTRICTIONS
Section 8.01. Transfer Restrictions.
(a) No Consenting First Lien Lender may sell, assign, transfer, hypothecate, pledge, grant a participation in, or otherwise dispose of (each, a "**[-transfer-] [+Transfer+]**") any of its First Lien Term Loan Claims unless such Transfer is to (i) another Consenting First Lien Lender or (ii) a Qualified Transferee that executes and delivers a Joinder to counsel for the Company and counsel for the Ad Hoc Group within [-five (5)-] [+ten (10)+] Business Days of such Transfer.
(b) Any Transfer in violation of this Section 8.01 shall be void ab initio, and the Company Parties and the other Consenting First Lien Lenders shall have the right to enforce the voiding of such Transfer. [+For the purposes of this Agreement, any such purported transferee shall not be deemed a Consenting First Lien Lender.+]
[+(c) Notwithstanding Section 8.01(a), each Consenting First Lien Lender may Transfer up to fifteen percent (15%) of its First Lien Term Loan Claims held as of the RSA Effective Date to any person that is not a Consenting First Lien Lender or a Qualified Transferee, without requiring such transferee to execute a Joinder (each, a "Permitted Transfer"); provided, that the aggregate amount of Permitted Transfers by all Consenting First Lien Lenders shall not exceed fifteen percent (15%) of the aggregate First Lien Term Loan Claims held by all Consenting First Lien Lenders as of the RSA Effective Date [ADDED: (as set forth on Schedule 2 hereto)].+]
Section 8.02. Qualified Transferee Joinder. Any Qualified Transferee shall execute and deliver a Joinder in substantially the form attached hereto as Exhibit D to counsel for the Company and counsel for the Ad Hoc Group within the time period specified in Section 8.01(a). Such Joinder [+shall be effective upon delivery and+] shall bind the Qualified Transferee to all of the terms, conditions, and obligations of this Agreement, and such Qualified Transferee shall be deemed a Consenting First Lien Lender for all purposes hereunder.
ARTICLE IX — TERMINATION
Section 9.01. Termination by Mutual Consent. This Agreement may be terminated at any time by mutual written consent of the Company and the Required Consenting Lenders.
Section 9.02. Termination by the Company. The Company may terminate this Agreement, upon written notice to counsel for the Ad Hoc Group, upon the occurrence of any of the following events:
(a) a material breach by the Required Consenting Lenders of any representation, warranty, covenant, or obligation contained in this Agreement that remains uncured for [-ten (10)-] [+five (5)+] Business Days after written notice thereof to counsel for the Ad Hoc Group;
(b) the conversion of any Chapter 11 Case to a case under chapter 7 of the Bankruptcy Code;
(c) the appointment of a chapter 11 trustee or an examiner with expanded powers beyond those set forth in section 1106(a)(3) and (4) of the Bankruptcy Code in any Chapter 11 Case;
(d) the dismissal of any Chapter 11 Case;
(e) the failure to satisfy any Milestone [-(subject to a ten (10) Business Day cure period)-] [+(subject to a five (5) Business Day cure period)+]; or
[+(f) the issuance by any governmental authority of any final, non-appealable order or decree making consummation of the Restructuring Transactions illegal or otherwise permanently preventing their consummation.+]
Section 9.03. Termination by the Required Consenting Lenders. The Required Consenting Lenders may terminate this Agreement, upon written notice to the Company, upon the occurrence of any of the following events:
(a) a material breach by any Company Party of any representation, warranty, covenant, or obligation contained in this Agreement that remains uncured for [-ten (10)-] [+five (5)+] Business Days after written notice thereof to the Company;
(b) the conversion of any Chapter 11 Case to a case under chapter 7 of the Bankruptcy Code;
(c) the appointment of a chapter 11 trustee or an examiner with expanded powers beyond those set forth in section 1106(a)(3) and (4) of the Bankruptcy Code in any Chapter 11 Case;
(d) the dismissal of any Chapter 11 Case;
(e) the failure to satisfy any Milestone [-(subject to a ten (10) Business Day cure period)-] [+(subject to a five (5) Business Day cure period)+];
(f) the failure to obtain approval of the DIP Facility [-within forty-five (45) days of the Petition Date-] [+on an interim basis within five (5) Business Days of the Petition Date or on a final basis within forty-five (45) days of the Petition Date+];
(g) the entry of an order by the Bankruptcy Court granting relief from the automatic stay with respect to any assets of the Company Parties [-having a material value-] [+having a value in excess of $10,000,000+];
[+(h) the Company's Liquidity (as defined in Section 1.01) falls below the Minimum Liquidity Threshold (i.e., the Company's trailing four (4)-week average Liquidity falls below $40,000,000) as of the last Business Day of any calendar week;+]
(i) the Company exercises the Fiduciary Out under Section 7.01; [+or+]
[+(j) any Company Party files any motion, pleading, or other document with the Bankruptcy Court that is materially inconsistent with this Agreement or the Restructuring Transactions without the prior written consent of the Required Consenting Lenders.+]
Section 9.04. Effect of Termination. Upon the termination of this Agreement pursuant to Section 9.01, 9.02, or 9.03, all obligations of the Parties under this Agreement shall terminate and be of no further force or effect, and no Party shall have any continuing liability to any other Party hereunder; provided, that (a) Section 9.04, Section 13.02, Section 13.03, Section 13.04, and Article X (solely with respect to any Releases that have become effective prior to the Termination Date) shall survive the termination of this Agreement; (b) termination shall not relieve any Party from liability for any willful breach of this Agreement occurring prior to such termination; and (c) [+termination shall not affect any claim or cause of action accruing prior to termination, and except for liability arising from any material breach of this Agreement occurring prior to such termination+]. No termination of this Agreement shall affect or limit the rights and remedies of any Party with respect to any breach of this Agreement occurring prior to the Termination Date.
ARTICLE X — RELEASES
Section 10.01. Mutual Releases. On the Effective Date, the Company Parties and the Consenting First Lien Lenders shall exchange mutual releases of all claims, causes of action, and liabilities arising prior to the Effective Date, in each case relating to or arising under the First Lien Credit Agreement, this Agreement, or the Restructuring Transactions, in favor of each other and their respective current and former officers, directors, managers, principals, members, employees, agents, financial advisors, attorneys, accountants, investment bankers, consultants, representatives, and other professionals (each in their capacity as such) (collectively, the "Released Parties"). Such releases shall be included in the Plan and the Confirmation Order and shall be effective on the Effective Date.
[+Section 10.02. Third-Party Releases. On the Effective Date, each holder of a Claim or Interest that (a) votes to accept the Plan, (b) is deemed to accept the Plan, (c) abstains from voting on the Plan, or (d) votes to reject the Plan but does not affirmatively opt out of the releases provided in the Plan by checking the appropriate box on the applicable ballot, shall be deemed to have conclusively, absolutely, unconditionally, irrevocably, and forever released and discharged the Released Parties from any and all claims, obligations, debts, rights, suits, damages, causes of action, remedies, and liabilities whatsoever, whether known or unknown, foreseen or unforeseen, matured or unmatured, existing or hereafter arising, in law, equity, contract, tort, or otherwise, based in whole or in part upon any act or omission, transaction, or other occurrence or circumstances existing or taking place prior to or on the Effective Date arising from or related in any way to the Debtors, the Chapter 11 Cases, the Plan, the Disclosure Statement, the Restructuring Transactions, or any document, instrument, or agreement (including this Agreement) relating to any of the foregoing. For the avoidance of doubt, the releases set forth in this Section 10.02 shall be binding on all holders of Claims and Interests, including those holders who do not vote on the Plan, subject only to the opt-out procedures set forth in the Plan. The releases contained in this Section 10.02 shall be set forth in the Plan and the Confirmation Order.+]
[+Section 10.03. Injunction. All entities who have held, hold, or may hold claims, obligations, suits, judgments, damages, demands, debts, rights, causes of action, or liabilities that are released pursuant to Section 10.01 or Section 10.02 are permanently enjoined, from and after the Effective Date, from (a) commencing or continuing in any manner any action or other proceeding of any kind against any Released Party on account of or in connection with or with respect to any such released claims, (b) enforcing, attaching, collecting, or recovering by any manner or means any judgment, award, decree, or order against any Released Party on account of or in connection with any such released claims, (c) creating, perfecting, or enforcing any encumbrance of any kind against any Released Party or against the property or estate of any Released Party on account of any such released claims, and (d) commencing or continuing in any manner any action or other proceeding of any kind against any Released Party that does not comply with or is inconsistent with the provisions of the Plan or the Confirmation Order.+]

ARTICLE XII — REPRESENTATIONS AND WARRANTIES
Section 12.01. Representations and Warranties of the Company Parties. Each Company Party [-represents and warrants-] [+hereby represents and warrants+], [+as of the date hereof and as of the RSA Effective Date,+] as follows:

17	**[I. Purpose and Background]{.underline}**
18	
19	This memorandum establishes the Company\'s negotiating framework in advance of the anticipated circulation of the draft Restructuring Support Agreement (the \"RSA\") to the Ad Hoc Group of First Lien Term Loan Lenders (the \"Ad Hoc Group\"). The current target for circulation of the RSA draft to counsel for the Ad Hoc Group is March 17, 2025. The purpose of this memorandum is to ensure that all members of the deal team are fully aligned on (a) the Company\'s non-negotiable positions (\"red lines\"), (b) areas of acceptable flexibility where concessions may be strategically offered, and (c) the strategic priorities that should guide the negotiation as a whole.
20	
21	The RSA is intended to serve as the foundation for an anticipated prepackaged Chapter 11 filing by Ridgeline Hospitality Group, Inc. (the \"Company\" or \"Ridgeline\") in the United States Bankruptcy Court for the District of Delaware. The target date for execution of the RSA is April 14, 2025. Under the Company\'s draft, the anticipated petition date is April 17, 2025, which falls five (5) business days after the RSA effective date. This timeline is driven by the Company\'s deteriorating liquidity position and looming debt maturities, as described below.
22	
23	Sternwick & Calloway LLP (lead partner: Jonathan M. Garvey), counsel to the Ad Hoc Group, and Clearbridge Advisory Group LLC (Managing Director: Thomas A. Birch), the Ad Hoc Group\'s financial advisor, have been engaged in preliminary discussions with our team regarding the broad framework for the restructuring. However, neither Sternwick & Calloway nor Clearbridge Advisory has yet seen a full RSA draft. To date, discussions have been limited to term sheets and high-level economic parameters.
24	
25	By way of brief background, Ridgeline Hospitality Group, Inc. is a Delaware corporation headquartered at 900 Lakeshore Boulevard, Suite 2400, Chicago, Illinois 60611. The Company operates 214 hotel properties across 31 states under three distinct brands: Ridgeline Suites, Aldersgate Hotels, and PeakStay Select. The Company employs approximately 11,400 individuals across its portfolio. For the fiscal year ended December 31, 2024, the Company reported consolidated revenue of approximately \$1.24 billion and consolidated EBITDA of approximately \$187.3 million.
26	
27	The Company faces a series of near-term debt maturities that necessitate a comprehensive restructuring:
28	
29	> • **ABL Revolving Credit Facility:** Maturity on June 15, 2025
30	>
31	> • **Senior Unsecured Notes:** Maturity on September 15, 2025
32	>
33	> • **First Lien Term Loan:** Maturity on December 15, 2025
34	>
35	> • **Second Lien Secured Notes:** Maturity on March 15, 2026
36	
37	Current liquidity stands at approximately \$113 million, consisting of \$68 million of unrestricted cash on hand and \$45 million of availability under the ABL Revolving Credit Facility (\$80 million currently drawn against a \$125 million commitment). This liquidity position, while adequate for near-term operations, is insufficient to address the approaching maturity wall without a comprehensive restructuring.
38	
39	It should be noted that the second lien secured noteholders, represented by Kelton Harris & Roe LLP, and the senior unsecured noteholders have not yet been engaged in RSA negotiations. The initial phase of negotiations will focus exclusively on reaching agreement with the Ad Hoc Group. Engagement with junior creditor constituencies will follow once the first lien framework is substantially agreed upon.
40	
41	**[II. Capital Structure Overview]{.underline}**
42	
43	For reference, the following is a summary of the Company\'s current capital structure:
44	
45	**ABL Revolving Credit Facility**
46	
47	> • Commitment: \$125 million
48	>
49	> • Outstanding: \$80 million drawn; \$45 million available
50	>
51	> • Administrative Agent: Briarwood Commercial Bank, N.A.
52	>
53	> • Maturity: June 15, 2025
54	>
55	> • Security: First-priority lien on ABL priority collateral (receivables, inventory, deposit accounts)

94

99

103
