137	**10.1 Adequate Protection for Pre-Petition First Lien Lenders**
138	As adequate protection for any diminution in value of the pre-petition first lien lenders\' interests in the pre-petition collateral resulting from the Debtors\' use of cash collateral and the priming of the pre-petition first lien term loan liens by the DIP liens, the pre-petition first lien term loan agent (Briarwood Commercial Bank, N.A.) and the first lien term loan lenders shall receive the following forms of adequate protection:
139	> \(a\) **Adequate Protection Replacement Liens:** Replacement liens on all DIP Collateral (other than the proceeds of avoidance actions under Chapter 5 of the Bankruptcy Code), which replacement liens shall be junior only to (i) the DIP liens, (ii) the Carveout, and (iii) any pre-petition liens that were validly perfected and senior in priority to the first lien term loan liens as of the Petition Date;
140	>
141	> \(b\) **Adequate Protection Superpriority Claims:** Allowed superpriority administrative expense claims under Section 507(b) of the Bankruptcy Code against each of the Debtors\' estates, which superpriority claims shall be junior only to the DIP superpriority claims, the Carveout, and any superpriority claims granted to holders of senior pre-petition liens;
142	>
143	> \(c\) **Adequate Protection Interest Payments:** Current cash payment of interest on the pre-petition first lien term loans at the non-default contract rate of SOFR plus 375 basis points per annum, payable monthly in arrears in accordance with the terms of the pre-petition First Lien Credit Agreement; and
144	>
145	> \(d\) **Agent Fees and Expenses:** Current cash payment of all reasonable and documented fees, costs, and out-of-pocket expenses of the pre-petition first lien term loan agent and its retained professionals incurred in connection with the Chapter 11 Cases and the DIP Facility.
146	**10.2 Adequate Protection for Second Lien Noteholders**
147	As adequate protection for any diminution in value of the second lien noteholders\' interests in the pre-petition collateral resulting from the priming of the second lien secured note liens by the DIP liens and the adequate protection replacement liens granted to the pre-petition first lien lenders, the second lien indenture trustee (Commonwealth National Trust Company) and the second lien noteholders shall receive the following forms of adequate protection:
148	> \(a\) **Adequate Protection Replacement Liens:** Replacement liens on all DIP Collateral (other than ABL priority collateral and the proceeds of avoidance actions under Chapter 5 of the Bankruptcy Code), which replacement liens shall be junior to (i) the DIP liens, (ii) the pre-petition first lien adequate protection replacement liens, (iii) the Carveout, and (iv) any pre-petition liens that were validly perfected and senior in priority to the second lien secured note liens as of the Petition Date; and
149	>
150	> \(b\) **Adequate Protection Superpriority Claims:** Allowed superpriority administrative expense claims under Section 507(b) of the Bankruptcy Code, which superpriority claims shall be junior to the DIP superpriority claims, the first lien adequate protection superpriority claims, and the Carveout.
151	No current cash interest payments shall be made to the second lien noteholders as adequate protection, consistent with the junior lien status of the second lien secured notes and the contemplated treatment of such claims under the Plan.
152	**10.3 ABL Facility**
153	The existing ABL revolving credit facility (with a commitment amount of \$125,000,000, of which approximately \$80,000,000 is currently drawn, agent: Briarwood Commercial Bank, N.A., stated maturity: June 15, 2025) shall continue in place during the Chapter 11 Cases or be replaced with a post-petition ABL facility on terms and conditions acceptable to the Required DIP Lenders in their reasonable discretion. ABL priority collateral (consisting of receivables, inventory, and certain deposit accounts) shall not be subject to DIP priming liens to the extent of the ABL priority claims, consistent with the terms of the existing intercreditor agreement among the pre-petition secured parties.
154	**[SECTION 11: CONDITIONS PRECEDENT]{.underline}**
155	**11.1 Conditions to Initial Funding (Interim Draw)**
156	The initial draw of the DIP Facility shall be subject to the satisfaction (or waiver by the Required DIP Lenders) of the following conditions precedent:
157	> \(a\) The RSA shall have been duly executed and delivered by the Company and Consenting First Lien Lenders holding at least 62.4% of the aggregate outstanding principal amount of first lien term loan claims, and shall be in full force and effect;
158	>
159	> \(b\) The Borrowers shall have filed voluntary petitions for relief under Chapter 11 of the Bankruptcy Code in the United States Bankruptcy Court for the District of Delaware;
160	>
161	> \(c\) The Bankruptcy Court shall have entered the Interim DIP Order, in form and substance acceptable to the Required DIP Lenders, the DIP Agent, and the Borrowers, authorizing the Borrowers to borrow up to \$100,000,000 under the DIP Facility on an interim basis and to use cash collateral;
162	>
163	> \(d\) The Borrowers shall have delivered the DIP Budget to the DIP Agent and each of the DIP Lenders, which DIP Budget shall be in form and substance reasonably acceptable to the Required DIP Lenders;
164	>
165	> \(e\) No Event of Default shall have occurred and be continuing, and no condition shall exist that, with the giving of notice or the passage of time (or both), would constitute an Event of Default;
166	>
167	> \(f\) The definitive DIP credit documentation, including the DIP credit agreement, security documents, and all ancillary agreements, shall have been executed and delivered in form and substance acceptable to the Required DIP Lenders, the DIP Agent, and the Borrowers;
168	>
169	> \(g\) All first-day motions and orders customary for Chapter 11 cases of this nature and size shall have been filed with the Bankruptcy Court and, to the extent necessary for the initial funding, entered by the Bankruptcy Court, including (without limitation) motions to pay employee wages and benefits, motions to pay critical vendors, and motions for joint administration;
170	>
171	> \(h\) The Borrowers shall have paid all reasonable and documented fees, costs, and out-of-pocket expenses of the DIP Agent, Sternwick & Calloway LLP (as counsel to the DIP Lenders), and Clearbridge Advisory Group LLC (as financial advisor to the DIP Lenders), in each case incurred through and including the Closing Date and for which invoices have been submitted;
172	>
173	> \(i\) All representations and warranties made by the Borrowers in the DIP documents shall be true and correct in all material respects (or, in the case of any representation qualified by materiality, in all respects) as of the Closing Date; and
174	>
175	> \(j\) The Borrowers shall have delivered to the DIP Agent and the DIP Lenders such other documents, certificates, and opinions as the DIP Agent or the Required DIP Lenders may reasonably request.
176	**11.2 Conditions to Final Draw**
177	In addition to the conditions set forth in Section 11.1 (other than clauses (b), (c), and (g) thereof, which are applicable only to the initial funding), the Final Draw shall be subject to the satisfaction (or waiver by the Required DIP Lenders) of the following additional conditions precedent:
178	> \(a\) The Bankruptcy Court shall have entered the Final DIP Order within forty-five (45) days of the Petition Date, in form and substance acceptable to the Required DIP Lenders, the DIP Agent, and the Borrowers;
179	>
180	> \(b\) The roll-up of \$75,000,000 of pre-petition first lien term loan claims as contemplated by Section 4 hereof shall have been completed in accordance with the Final DIP Order;
181	>
182	> \(c\) No material adverse change shall have occurred in the business, operations, assets, liabilities, or financial condition of the Debtors (taken as a whole) since the Petition Date; and
183	>
184	> \(d\) An updated DIP Budget shall have been delivered to and accepted by the Required DIP Lenders.
185	**[SECTION 12: REPRESENTATIONS AND WARRANTIES]{.underline}**
186	The Borrowers shall make customary representations and warranties in the definitive DIP credit documentation, including without limitation representations and warranties with respect to the following matters:
187	> \(a\) corporate organization, valid existence, and good standing of each Borrower in its jurisdiction of organization and in each jurisdiction where the conduct of its business or the ownership of its properties requires such qualification;
188	>
189	> \(b\) corporate power and authority to execute, deliver, and perform the DIP documents, and the due authorization, execution, and delivery thereof, and the enforceability of the DIP documents against each Borrower in accordance with their terms (subject to customary bankruptcy and equitable principles exceptions);
190	>
191	> \(c\) no conflict between the DIP documents and the organizational documents, material agreements, or applicable laws binding on the Borrowers (including the pre-petition First Lien Credit Agreement and the Second Lien Notes Indenture);
192	>
193	> \(d\) accuracy and completeness in all material respects of all financial statements, projections, and the DIP Budget delivered to the DIP Agent and the DIP Lenders;
194	>
195	> \(e\) validity, enforceability, perfection, and priority of the DIP liens on the DIP Collateral;
196	>
197	> \(f\) absence of undisclosed material liabilities, material litigation, or pending or threatened material governmental proceedings not previously disclosed in writing to the DIP Lenders;
198	>
199	> \(g\) compliance in all material respects with applicable environmental laws and the absence of material environmental liabilities;
200	>
201	> \(h\) compliance with ERISA and the absence of material unfunded pension liabilities or ERISA events;
202	>
203	> \(i\) ownership of or valid licenses to all intellectual property material to the Debtors\' business;
204	>
205	> \(j\) maintenance of insurance coverage in amounts and types customary for similarly situated companies;
206	>
207	> \(k\) compliance with all applicable sanctions laws administered by OFAC, anti-money laundering laws (including the Bank Secrecy Act and the USA PATRIOT Act), and anti-corruption laws (including the Foreign Corrupt Practices Act); and
208	>
209	> \(l\) the Company operates 214 hotel properties across 31 states with approximately 11,400 employees as of the date hereof.
210	**[SECTION 13: AFFIRMATIVE COVENANTS]{.underline}**
211	The Borrowers shall comply with customary affirmative covenants in the definitive DIP credit documentation, including without limitation the following:
212	> \(a\) compliance with the DIP Budget, subject to the permitted variances described in Section 7.1;
213	>
214	> \(b\) maintenance of insurance coverage on all material properties and assets in amounts, types, and with insurers reasonably satisfactory to the DIP Agent;
215	>
216	> \(c\) compliance in all material respects with all applicable laws, regulations, and governmental orders, including applicable environmental, labor, and tax laws;
217	>
218	> \(d\) preservation of corporate existence, material rights, franchises, licenses, and permits;
219	>
220	> \(e\) payment when due of all taxes, assessments, and governmental charges, except to the extent contested in good faith by appropriate proceedings and for which adequate reserves have been established;
221	>
222	> \(f\) maintenance of proper books of account and records consistent with past practices and generally accepted accounting principles;
223	>
224	> \(g\) access and inspection rights, permitting the DIP Agent and the DIP Lenders (and their respective advisors and consultants) to have reasonable access to the Debtors\' properties, books, records, and management personnel upon reasonable prior notice during normal business hours;
225	>
226	> \(h\) compliance in all respects with the DIP Orders, including all terms, conditions, and requirements set forth therein;
227	>
228	> \(i\) use of all proceeds of the DIP Facility solely for the permitted purposes described in Section 2.2;
229	>
230	> \(j\) delivery of all financial reports and other information required pursuant to Section 7.2 within the time periods specified therein;
231	>
232	> \(k\) full cooperation with the DIP Agent\'s lien perfection requirements, including executing and delivering all instruments, agreements, and documents reasonably requested by the DIP Agent in connection with the perfection and maintenance of the DIP liens; and
233	>
234	> \(l\) continued operation of the Ridgeline Suites, Aldersgate Hotels, and PeakStay Select brand portfolios in the ordinary course of business, consistent with past practice and the DIP Budget.
235	**[SECTION 14: NEGATIVE COVENANTS]{.underline}**
236	The Borrowers shall be subject to customary negative covenants in the definitive DIP credit documentation, including without limitation the following:
237	> \(a\) **Liens.** No Borrower shall create, incur, assume, or permit to exist any lien on any DIP Collateral, other than (i) the DIP liens, (ii) the adequate protection replacement liens authorized by the DIP Orders, (iii) liens permitted under the existing pre-petition credit documents and the existing intercreditor agreement, and (iv) other liens customarily permitted in DIP credit facilities (collectively, \"Permitted Liens\");
238	>
239	> \(b\) **Indebtedness.** No Borrower shall incur, create, assume, or permit to exist any indebtedness, other than (i) obligations under the DIP Facility, (ii) post-petition trade payables incurred in the ordinary course of business, (iii) obligations under any post-petition ABL facility approved by the Required DIP Lenders, and (iv) other indebtedness customarily permitted in DIP credit facilities;
240	>
241	> \(c\) **Asset Dispositions.** No Borrower shall sell, transfer, lease, or otherwise dispose of any assets outside the ordinary course of business, subject to a de minimis threshold of \$5,000,000 in the aggregate without the consent of the Required DIP Lenders, and Bankruptcy Court approval shall be required for any individual disposition or series of related dispositions with a value exceeding \$10,000,000;
242	>
243	> \(d\) **Investments and Capital Expenditures.** No Borrower shall make any investment, acquisition, or capital expenditure outside the DIP Budget, except with a permitted variance of 10% of the aggregate amount budgeted for capital expenditures in any applicable four-week period;
244	>
245	> \(e\) **Affiliate Transactions.** No Borrower shall enter into any transaction with any affiliate or insider outside the ordinary course of business and on terms not less favorable than would be obtained in an arm\'s-length transaction with a non-affiliated party;
246	>
247	> \(f\) **Plan and RSA Modifications.** No Borrower shall amend, modify, supplement, or waive any provision of the Plan or the RSA, in each case without the prior written consent of the Required DIP Lenders;
248	>
249	> \(g\) **Pre-Petition Claims.** No Borrower shall pay, satisfy, or otherwise discharge any pre-petition claim or obligation except as authorized by applicable orders of the Bankruptcy Court (including first-day relief orders authorizing the payment of employee wages and benefits, critical vendor claims, and similar relief); and
250	>
251	> \(h\) **Minimum Liquidity Covenant.** The Borrowers shall maintain at all times minimum total liquidity (defined as the sum of (i) unrestricted cash and cash equivalents on hand and (ii) availability under any post-petition revolving credit facility) of not less than Thirty Million Dollars (\$30,000,000). For purposes of this covenant, liquidity shall be calculated as of the end of each business day and tested weekly in connection with the delivery of the weekly liquidity schedule required under Section 7.2(a)(iii).
252	**[SECTION 15: EVENTS OF DEFAULT]{.underline}**
253	**15.1 Events of Default**
254	The occurrence of any of the following events shall constitute an event of default under the DIP Facility (each, an \"Event of Default\"):
255	> \(a\) **Payment Default.** Failure by any Borrower to make any payment of principal or interest on the DIP obligations when due and payable (whether at stated maturity, upon acceleration, or otherwise), with no grace period;
256	>
257	> \(b\) **Representation Breach.** Any representation or warranty made by any Borrower in the DIP documents shall prove to have been incorrect in any material respect when made or deemed made, with no cure period;
258	>
259	> \(c\) **Reporting Covenant Breach.** Failure by any Borrower to comply with any financial reporting covenant under Section 7 of this Term Sheet, if such failure is not cured within five (5) business days after written notice thereof from the DIP Agent;
260	>
261	> \(d\) **Budget Variance Breach.** Failure by the Borrowers to satisfy the DIP Budget variance requirements under Section 7.1 (including the Receipt Variance or the Disbursement Variance), if such failure is not cured in the subsequent four-week testing period;
262	>
263	> \(e\) **Other Covenant Breach.** Failure by any Borrower to comply with any other covenant or agreement contained in the DIP documents (other than those specifically addressed in clauses (a) through (d) above), if such failure is not cured within ten (10) business days after written notice thereof from the DIP Agent;
264	>
265	> \(f\) **Milestone Failure.** Failure to satisfy any milestone set forth in Section 8.1, subject to the ten (10) business day cure period set forth in Section 8.2;
266	>
267	> \(g\) **Conversion to Chapter 7.** Entry of an order by the Bankruptcy Court or any other court of competent jurisdiction converting any of the Chapter 11 Cases to a case under Chapter 7 of the Bankruptcy Code;
268	>
269	> \(h\) **Trustee or Examiner Appointment.** Entry of an order appointing a trustee under Chapter 11 of the Bankruptcy Code in any of the Chapter 11 Cases or appointing an examiner with expanded powers beyond those set forth in Sections 1106(a)(3) and 1106(a)(4) of the Bankruptcy Code;
270	>
271	> \(i\) **Case Dismissal.** Entry of an order dismissing any of the Chapter 11 Cases, or any Borrower filing a motion or otherwise seeking the dismissal of any of the Chapter 11 Cases;
272	>
273	> \(j\) **Stay Relief.** Entry of an order granting relief from the automatic stay imposed by Section 362 of the Bankruptcy Code with respect to any material asset or group of assets of any Borrower having a value in excess of \$10,000,000;
274	>
275	> \(k\) **RSA Termination.** Termination of the RSA in accordance with its terms;
276	>
277	> \(l\) **DIP Order Modification.** Entry of any order reversing, amending, supplementing, staying, vacating, or otherwise modifying any DIP Order in a manner that is adverse to the DIP Lenders or the DIP Agent, without the prior written consent of the Required DIP Lenders;
278	>
279	> \(m\) **Cross-Default.** A default or event of default under any material indebtedness (including, for the avoidance of doubt, any post-petition ABL facility) of any Borrower in an aggregate principal amount in excess of \$10,000,000, to the extent such default or event of default results in the acceleration of such indebtedness or the commencement of enforcement proceedings;
280	>
281	> \(n\) **DIP Order Effectiveness.** Any DIP Order shall cease to be in full force and effect, or shall be the subject of a pending appeal, motion to vacate, or stay (whether by the Bankruptcy Court, any appellate court, or otherwise); and
282	>
283	> \(o\) **Minimum Liquidity Breach.** The Borrowers\' total liquidity (as defined in Section 14(h)) falls below \$30,000,000 at any time.
284	**15.2 Remedies.** Upon the occurrence and during the continuance of an Event of Default, the Required DIP Lenders (acting through the DIP Agent) may, subject to the Carveout and any applicable notice periods set forth in the DIP Orders:
285	> \(a\) declare all outstanding DIP obligations immediately due and payable, without presentment, demand, protest, or other notice of any kind, all of which are expressly waived by the Borrowers;
286	>
287	> \(b\) terminate any and all unfunded DIP commitments; and
288	>
289	> \(c\) exercise any and all rights and remedies available under the DIP documents, the DIP Orders, the Bankruptcy Code, the Uniform Commercial Code, or any other applicable law, including the right to foreclose on the DIP Collateral.
290	Notwithstanding the foregoing, the DIP Agent shall provide not less than five (5) business days\' prior written notice to counsel for the Borrowers, counsel for any official committee of unsecured creditors, and the United States Trustee before exercising remedies against the DIP Collateral, unless such notice period is waived or shortened by the Bankruptcy Court. During such notice period, the Borrowers, any committee, and the U.S. Trustee shall have the opportunity to seek relief from the Bankruptcy Court.
291	**[SECTION 16: INDEMNIFICATION]{.underline}**
292	The Borrowers shall indemnify, defend, and hold harmless the DIP Agent, each DIP Lender, and their respective affiliates, partners, members, directors, officers, employees, agents, advisors, attorneys, accountants, consultants, and controlling persons (each, an \"Indemnified Party\") from and against any and all losses, claims, damages, liabilities, costs, and related expenses (including reasonable and documented attorneys\' fees and disbursements of one primary counsel and, if necessary, one local counsel in each relevant jurisdiction, and one firm of specialists for each relevant specialty), arising out of, resulting from, or in connection with (a) the DIP Facility or any other DIP document, (b) the use or proposed use of the proceeds of the DIP Facility, (c) any actual or threatened claim, action, suit, proceeding, or investigation relating to any of the foregoing, or (d) any actual or alleged presence or release of hazardous materials on, at, or under any property currently or formerly owned, leased, or operated by any Debtor; except, in each case, to the extent that such losses, claims, damages, liabilities, costs, or expenses are determined by a final, non-appealable judgment of a court of competent jurisdiction to have resulted from such Indemnified Party\'s gross negligence, willful misconduct, or material breach of its obligations under the DIP documents.
293	**[SECTION 17: GOVERNING LAW AND JURISDICTION]{.underline}**
294	The DIP credit agreement, this Term Sheet, and all other DIP documents shall be governed by and construed in accordance with the laws of the State of New York, without regard to principles of conflicts of law that would result in the application of the laws of any other jurisdiction. The Bankruptcy Court shall have exclusive jurisdiction over all matters arising out of or relating to the DIP documents and the transactions contemplated hereby, including all disputes between and among the parties hereto. To the extent that the Bankruptcy Court is unable or declines to hear any such dispute, the parties hereby irrevocably consent to the non-exclusive jurisdiction of the United States District Court for the District of Delaware, and any appellate court therefrom, for the resolution of such disputes. Each party hereto irrevocably waives any objection to venue in the foregoing courts and any claim that any such action or proceeding has been brought in an inconvenient forum.
295	**[SECTION 18: MISCELLANEOUS]{.underline}**
296	**18.1 Required DIP Lenders**
297	\"Required DIP Lenders\" shall mean, at any time, DIP Lenders holding in the aggregate more than 50% of the total outstanding DIP obligations at such time (including, for the avoidance of doubt, the Rolled-Up Claims following the effectiveness of the roll-up pursuant to Section 4).
298	**18.2 Assignments.** DIP Lenders may assign their DIP commitments and loans (in whole or in part) to other DIP Lenders, to affiliates of DIP Lenders, or to qualified institutional buyers (as defined under Rule 144A of the Securities Act of 1933, as amended), in each case subject to (a) the prior written consent of the DIP Agent (not to be unreasonably withheld, conditioned, or delayed), (b) the transfer restrictions and joinder requirements set forth in the RSA, and (c) minimum assignment amounts to be specified in the definitive DIP credit documentation. No assignment shall be made to any person that is a Disqualified Lender (as such term shall be defined in the definitive DIP credit documentation to include competitors of the Debtors and certain other persons identified by the Borrowers). The DIP Agent shall maintain a register of all DIP Lenders and their respective commitments and outstanding loans.
299	**18.3 Amendments and Waivers**
300	Any amendment, modification, supplement, or waiver of any provision of the DIP documents shall require the prior written consent of the Borrowers and the Required DIP Lenders; provided, however, that the following \"sacred right\" provisions shall require the consent of each DIP Lender directly and adversely affected thereby: (a) any reduction in the principal amount of the DIP obligations; (b) any reduction in the Applicable Rate or any fees payable under the DIP Facility; (c) any extension of the Maturity Date; (d) any modification of the Carveout; (e) any modification of the roll-up provisions set forth in Section 4; (f) any modification of the definition of \"Required DIP Lenders\"; and (g) any release of all or substantially all of the DIP Collateral or all or substantially all of the guarantees of the DIP obligations.
301	**18.4 Expenses.** The Borrowers shall pay, promptly upon demand, all reasonable and documented out-of-pocket costs, fees, and expenses incurred by the DIP Agent and the DIP Lenders (including the fees and disbursements of Sternwick & Calloway LLP, as counsel to the DIP Lenders, and Clearbridge Advisory Group LLC, as financial advisor to the DIP Lenders) in connection with the negotiation, preparation, execution, delivery, administration, interpretation, amendment, modification, enforcement, protection, and collection of the DIP Facility and all related DIP documents, including in connection with any workout, restructuring, or enforcement proceedings. Payment of such amounts shall be a condition precedent to the initial funding of the DIP Facility as set forth in Section 11.1(h).
302	**18.5 Confidentiality and Publicity**
303	The terms and conditions of the DIP Facility, this Term Sheet, and all related DIP documents are subject to the confidentiality provisions set forth in the RSA. Any public disclosure of the DIP Facility or the terms hereof shall be made in a manner consistent with the RSA and applicable securities laws, including any required filings under the Securities Exchange Act of 1934 and the rules and regulations of the Securities and Exchange Commission.
304	**18.6 Entire Agreement**
305	This Term Sheet, together with the RSA and the exhibits and schedules thereto, constitutes the entire agreement among the parties hereto with respect to the subject matter hereof and supersedes all prior and contemporaneous agreements, understandings, negotiations, and discussions, whether oral or written, of the parties relating to such subject matter. This Term Sheet is subject to, and shall be superseded in its entirety by, the definitive DIP credit documentation to be negotiated in good faith among the Borrowers, the DIP Agent, and the DIP Lenders and to be consistent in all material respects with the terms and conditions set forth herein.
306	**18.7 Counterparts.** This Term Sheet may be executed in one or more counterparts, each of which when so executed and delivered shall be deemed an original and all of which, taken together, shall constitute one and the same instrument. Delivery of an executed counterpart of this Term Sheet (or a signature page hereto) by facsimile transmission or by electronic mail in portable document format (.pdf) shall be equally as effective as delivery of an original executed counterpart of this Term Sheet.
307	**ACKNOWLEDGMENT AND AGREEMENT**
308	The undersigned parties hereby acknowledge and agree that this Term Sheet accurately reflects the proposed terms and conditions of the DIP Facility as of the date first written above, and that the parties shall negotiate in good faith to execute and deliver definitive DIP credit documentation consistent with the terms set forth herein. This acknowledgment does not constitute a binding commitment to provide financing except to the extent this Term Sheet is incorporated into the RSA and the RSA has become effective.
309	**IN WITNESS WHEREOF**, the parties hereto have caused this Term Sheet to be executed by their duly authorized representatives as of the date first written above.
310	**RIDGELINE HOSPITALITY GROUP, INC.** as Borrower, on behalf of itself and each of the other Borrowers
311	By: **\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_**
312	Name: David R. Nakamura
313	Title: Chief Financial Officer
314	Date: **\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_**
315	**BRIARWOOD COMMERCIAL BANK, N.A.** as DIP Administrative Agent
316	By: **\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_**
317	Name: **\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_**
318	Title: **\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_**
319	Date: **\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_**
320	**CONSENTING FIRST LIEN LENDERS / DIP LENDERS** severally and not jointly
321	\[Signature pages for each DIP Lender to be attached hereto\]
322	*Signature pages to this Term Sheet are for acknowledgment of the proposed terms set forth herein only and shall not constitute binding commitments. Definitive DIP credit documentation to be negotiated and executed in accordance with the RSA.*

from docx import Document
from docx.shared import Pt, Inches, RGBColor

from docx.enum.table import WD_TABLE_ALIGNMENT
from docx.enum.section import WD_ORIENT
from docx.oxml.ns import qn
from docx.oxml import OxmlElement

doc = Document()
sec = doc.sections[0]
sec.page_width = Inches(8.5); sec.page_height = Inches(11)
for m in ("left_margin","right_margin"): setattr(sec, m, Inches(1))
sec.top_margin = Inches(0.9); sec.bottom_margin = Inches(0.9)

st = doc.styles["Normal"]
st.font.name = "Times New Roman"; st.font.size = Pt(11)
st.element.rPr.rFonts.set(qn("w:eastAsia"), "Times New Roman")
st.paragraph_format.space_after = Pt(6)
for lvl, size in ((1, 13), (2, 12), (3, 11)):
    h = doc.styles["Heading %d" % lvl]
    h.font.name = "Times New Roman"; h.font.size = Pt(size); h.font.bold = True
    h.font.color.rgb = RGBColor(0x1F, 0x2A, 0x44)
    h.element.rPr.rFonts.set(qn("w:eastAsia"), "Times New Roman")
    h.paragraph_format.space_before = Pt(12 if lvl == 1 else 8)
    h.paragraph_format.space_after = Pt(4)
    h.paragraph_format.keep_with_next = True

def shade(cell, hexcolor):
    tcPr = cell._tc.get_or_add_tcPr()
    shd = OxmlElement("w:shd"); shd.set(qn("w:val"), "clear"); shd.set(qn("w:color"), "auto"); shd.set(qn("w:fill"), hexcolor)
    tcPr.append(shd)

def add_runs(p, text, size=None, bold_all=False, italic=False):
    # supports **bold** segments
    parts = text.split("**")
    for i, seg in enumerate(parts):
        if not seg: continue
        r = p.add_run(seg)
        r.bold = bold_all or (i % 2 == 1)
        r.italic = italic
        if size: r.font.size = Pt(size)
    return p

def para(text, bold=False, italic=False, align=None, size=None, after=None, indent=None):
    p = doc.add_paragraph()
    add_runs(p, text, size=size, bold_all=bold, italic=italic)
    if align == "center": p.alignment = WD_ALIGN_PARAGRAPH.CENTER
    elif align == "justify": p.alignment = WD_ALIGN_PARAGRAPH.JUSTIFY
    if after is not None: p.paragraph_format.space_after = Pt(after)
    if indent: p.paragraph_format.left_indent = Inches(indent)
    return p

def bullet(text, level=0):
    p = doc.add_paragraph(style="List Bullet" if level == 0 else "List Bullet 2")
    add_runs(p, text)
    p.paragraph_format.space_after = Pt(3)
    return p

def num(text):
    p = doc.add_paragraph(style="List Number")
    add_runs(p, text); p.paragraph_format.space_after = Pt(3)
    return p

def h(text, lvl=1):
    return doc.add_heading(text, level=lvl)

def table(headers, rows, widths=None, size=9, header_fill="1F2A44", zebra=True):
    t = doc.add_table(rows=1, cols=len(headers))
    t.style = "Table Grid"
    t.alignment = WD_TABLE_ALIGNMENT.CENTER
    hdr = t.rows[0].cells
    for i, x in enumerate(headers):
        hdr[i].text = ""
        p = hdr[i].paragraphs[0]
        r = p.add_run(x); r.bold = True; r.font.size = Pt(size); r.font.color.rgb = RGBColor(0xFF, 0xFF, 0xFF)
        shade(hdr[i], header_fill)
    # repeat header row
    trPr = t.rows[0]._tr.get_or_add_trPr()
    th = OxmlElement("w:tblHeader"); th.set(qn("w:val"), "true"); trPr.append(th)
    for ri, row in enumerate(rows):
        cells = t.add_row().cells
        for i, x in enumerate(row):
            cells[i].text = ""
            lines = str(x).split("\n")
            for li, line in enumerate(lines):
                p = cells[i].paragraphs[0] if li == 0 else cells[i].add_paragraph()
                p.paragraph_format.space_after = Pt(1)
                add_runs(p, line, size=size)
            if zebra and ri % 2 == 1: shade(cells[i], "EEF1F6")
    if widths:
        for row in t.rows:
            for i, w in enumerate(widths):
                row.cells[i].width = Inches(w)
    doc.add_paragraph().paragraph_format.space_after = Pt(2)
    return t
EOF

para("ASHFORD PIERCE LLP", bold=True, align="center", size=14, after=0)
para("MEMORANDUM", bold=True, align="center", size=12)
table(["", ""], [
 ["TO:", "Claire E. Vasquez, Partner"],
 ["CC:", "Susan K. Pratt, General Counsel, Ridgeline Hospitality Group, Inc.; David R. Nakamura, Chief Financial Officer; Allison W. Cheng, Managing Director, Pendleton Hargrave & Co. (economic sections)"],
 ["FROM:", "Ridgeline Restructuring Deal Team (Associate Team)"],
 ["DATE:", "April 3, 2025"],
 ["RE:", "Ridgeline Hospitality Group, Inc. — Analysis of the Ad Hoc Group’s April 2, 2025 Markup of the Restructuring Support Agreement; Economic Impact, Red-Line Issues, and Recommended Responses"],
], widths=[0.8, 5.7], size=10, header_fill="FFFFFF", zebra=False)

h("I. Executive Summary")
para("Sternwick & Calloway’s April 2 markup (the “**Markup**”) of our March 17 RSA draft (the “**Company Draft**”) is not an executable basis for the RSA. Measured against the March 14 Negotiating Framework memorandum (the “**Framework**”), the Markup crosses **25 of the 26** red-line or limit positions catalogued in Framework §VII; the only one it does not cross (the 3-business-day filing milestone) sits exactly at our floor. It also contains a number of significant changes that are untracked or that the cover email does not mention, and the cover email misdescribes several of the tracked changes. Our principal conclusions:", align="justify")
bullet("**Economics move decisively to the first lien, and within the first lien to the DIP-lending members.** On Pendleton Hargrave’s April 2 schedule, pro forma equity value falls from $502.5M to $341.25M (–$161.25M, a constant reduction at every TEV), second lien recovery falls from 15.9% to 7.2% and unsecured recovery from 10.1% to 4.6% (base TEV $1.3B), and MIP value roughly halves ($50.3M to $25.6M). On Pendleton’s methodology the Markup actually **lowers** total first lien class recovery ($956.8M to $921.2M) while adding $8.75M of DIP fees and ~$1.3M of incremental DIP interest payable only to the DIP lenders — a point we can use with the 37.6% of first lien holders outside the Ad Hoc Group. (We believe the schedule overstates the value leakage and recommend a re-run; see Part III.B.)")
bullet("**Undisclosed economic change: the unsecured warrants were cut** from 3% struck at $1.3B TEV to 2% struck at $1.4B TEV (Markup §6.04(b); Term Sheet). The cover email does not mention it and Pendleton’s schedule records the warrants as “unchanged.”")
bullet("**The 2.5% equity gap.** The Markup’s equity table states a 100% total, but 78% + 8% + 4% + 7.5% = 97.5%. The cover email says the “remaining 10%” is “reserved for the MIP and rights offering backstop,” but neither document contains a rights offering or backstop. This is precisely the “unallocated equity / rights offering pool” scenario the Framework (§IV.A) told us to watch for.")
bullet("**Structural provisions that would make the RSA a one-way option for the lenders:** (i) deletion (untracked) of the lenders’ covenant not to exercise remedies, plus a new §13.12 reserving the right to enforce remedies, **credit bid in a §363 sale**, and object to filings, alongside a tracked change to the recitals contemplating a “plan of reorganization **or liquidation**”; (ii) a permitted-transfer basket of 15% with no joinder, which could cut locked-up first lien support from 62.4% to ~53.0% of the class; (iii) a hair-trigger termination architecture (compressed milestones, 5-business-day cures, extensions only in the lenders’ “sole and absolute discretion,” a $40M trailing liquidity trigger with no cure, a new termination right for any “materially inconsistent” filing, and new flat MAC and “Solvency” representations brought down at the RSA Effective Date); and (iv) the untracked deletion of the Company’s right to terminate if the DIP lenders fail to fund.")
bullet("**Fiduciary out effectively disabled** (10-business-day notice; mandatory disclosure of the counterparty and terms; a 15% numerical “better recovery” hurdle; a 15-business-day match with information parity; and an untracked change from “consultation with” to “written advice of” counsel). Every element crosses a hard red line in Framework §III.A.")
bullet("**Pre-petition board observers** with notice, board materials and attendance while the lenders keep trading. The Framework treats this as non-negotiable (§IV.C, §VII), and the provision raises equitable subordination, insider/MNPI, privilege-waiver and confidentiality concerns, including the observers being in the room for any fiduciary-out deliberations.")
bullet("**Third-party releases** that bind abstaining, deemed-accepting and rejecting holders unless they opt out, and that bind “all holders of Claims and Interests.” After *Harrington v. Purdue Pharma L.P.*, 603 U.S. 204 (2024), non-consensual third-party releases are not available in chapter 11, and Delaware practice on opt-out “consent” is unsettled. As drafted, the provision is a confirmation risk that the Markup then turns into a milestone and termination risk.")
para("**Recommended posture.** We recommend that the Company (1) send a short process note reserving rights and asking Sternwick to (a) re-run the redline against our March 17 draft (the Markup was evidently compared against a different base; see Part II.B) and (b) answer the clarification items in Part VII; (2) brief the Board, through Ms. Pratt and Ms. Holloway, before any movement on a red-line item (Framework §III, §VI.6); and (3) respond with a Company turn and issues list that **uses the Framework’s flexibility as currency**: 1L equity up to 75% (2L 10% / unsecured 5%), exit term loan up to $625M, DIP pricing up to SOFR + 725, DIP fees capped at $3M, a DIP-to-exit conversion of up to $100M, a 7-business-day joinder window, a lender-majority post-emergence board, and acceptance of the 3-business-day filing milestone. In exchange we should require withdrawal of the observer rights, §13.12 and the permitted-transfer basket, restoration of the fiduciary out, carveout, MIP and milestone positions, and a consensual-only release construct. Part VI sets out the proposed package and fallbacks.", align="justify")

h("II. Documents Reviewed; Reliability of the Markup")
h("A. Documents", 2)
for t in [
 "Company Draft RSA (Ashford Pierce, March 17, 2025), including Exhibit A (Restructuring Term Sheet), Exhibit B (DIP summary), Exhibit C (Joinder), Schedules 1–2.",
 "Ad Hoc Group Markup of the RSA (Sternwick & Calloway, April 2, 2025), including revised Exhibits A–D and Schedules 1–2.",
 "Company DIP Facility Term Sheet dated March 17, 2025 (Exhibit B as circulated) (the “**DIP Term Sheet**”).",
 "Transmittal email from Jonathan M. Garvey to Claire E. Vasquez dated April 2, 2025, and the March 17 cover email (the “**Cover Email**”).",
 "Pendleton Hargrave Capital Structure Summary & Recovery Analysis (March 17, updated April 2, 2025) (the “**Pendleton Schedule**”).",
 "Ashford Pierce Negotiating Framework memorandum dated March 14, 2025 (the “**Framework**”)."]:
    bullet(t)
h("B. The Markup’s tracked changes are not a reliable comparison against our draft", 2)
para("The Cover Email describes “approximately 47 changes, the substantial majority of which are conforming, clarifying, or definitional.” That description is not reliable, and the Markup should be treated as a new draft rather than as a redline of ours:", align="justify")
bullet("**Different base document.** The Markup is organized in Articles I–XIII with different defined terms (e.g., “Consenting First Lien Lenders,” “Pro Forma Equity Interests,” Exhibit D Joinder), and its struck text frequently does not appear in the Company Draft at all. Examples: “$75,000,000 of the DIP Facility commitments shall be rolled up into the Exit Facility” (our draft rolls up $75M of **prepetition** first lien claims into the DIP; Company Draft §2.03, DIP Term Sheet §4.1); budget updates “every four (4) weeks” (our RSA term sheet says bi-weekly); stay relief “having a material value” (our §6.02(g) says $25,000,000); and a Default Rate of “SOFR + 850” (consistent with our DIP Term Sheet but not stated in the RSA).")
bullet("**Untracked substantive changes.** Our side-by-side review found at least 20 substantive differences from the Company Draft that carry no revision marks (catalogued in Part IV.J). They include the deletion of the lenders’ no-remedies covenant, the Company’s DIP-funding termination right, the release carve-outs for fraud, willful misconduct and gross negligence, the competitor exclusion from “Qualified Transferee,” the management-continuity covenant and the Section 13(d) “no group” acknowledgment, and the shrinking of Schedule 1 from ten Company Parties to four.")
bullet("**Mischaracterizations in the Cover Email** (detailed in Part V.A). Examples: the MIP is described as “up from 5%” when it was cut from 10% to 7.5%; the observer rights are described as running “between RSA execution and emergence” when Markup §11.02 ends them on the Petition Date; and the warrant cut, the carveout reduction, the liquidity trigger and the §13.12 reservation are not mentioned at all.")
para("**Recommendation:** Ask Sternwick for a full comparison against the March 17 Ashford Pierce draft, and run our own compare in parallel. Our turn should go back as a redline against **our** March 17 draft so that every departure is visible to the Board and, later, to the Court and the U.S. Trustee.", align="justify")
EOF

 "Transmittal email from Jonathan M. Garvey to Claire E. Vasquez dated April 2, 2025, and the March 17 cover email (the “**Cover Email**”).",

para("The Cover Email describes “approximately 47 changes, the substantial majority of which are conforming, clarifying, or definitional.” That description is not reliable, and the Markup should be treated as a new draft rather than as a redline of ours:", align="justify")

Our turn should go back as a redline against **our** March 17 draft so that every departure is visible to the Board and, later, to the Court and the U.S. Trustee.", align="justify")
EOF

S=/home/user/Lawless_Research_Lab/harvey_lab/sbx.sh; R=/home/user/Lawless_Research_Lab/harvey_lab/vendor/harvey-labs/results/bankruptcy-restructuring/analyze-counterparty-markup-of-restructuring-support-agreement/claude-code-session/20261016-040607; $S $R 'cat > /workspace/gen/p4.py <<"EOF"
h("IV. Issue-by-Issue Analysis and Recommended Responses")
para("Each change is classified against the Framework as **RED** (a red-line item under Framework §III or a “must not” limit), **FLEX** (an area of flexibility under Framework §IV), or **NEW** (not addressed in the Framework). Responses are Accept, Reject, or Counter. Section references are to the Markup unless noted (“CD” = Company Draft; “DIP TS” = March 17 DIP Term Sheet). Proposed rider language for the key counters is in Appendix B.", align="justify")
W = [1.15, 1.95, 1.95, 1.45]
HD = ["Provision / Class", "Change (CD → Markup)", "Assessment", "Recommended Response"]

h("A. Plan Economics", 2)
table(HD, [
 ["A1. 1L treatment
§6.02; Ex. A
RED / FLEX", "Exit TL $595M → $655M (55% of face); 1L equity 72% → 78%.", "Both exceed the Framework limits ($650M; 75%). Exit TL alone reaches 3.50x; with the rolled DIP, total exit debt is $830M (4.43x). The Markup does not specify exit TL pricing, maturity or covenants.", "**Counter:** 75% equity; exit TL $625M (hold $650M as Board-approved fallback). Add exit TL key terms to Ex. A."],
 ["A2. 2L treatment
§6.03
FLEX", "12% → 8% of equity.", "Below the 10% level at which the Framework expects contested confirmation/§1129(b) cramdown. Recovery of 7.2% vs. a 28-cent trading price invites a valuation fight.", "**Counter:** 10% (only as part of the 75% 1L package). Engage Kelton Harris & Roe (Part VI.C)."],
 ["A3. Unsecured treatment
§6.04(a)
FLEX", "6% → 4% of equity.", "Below the 5% level at which the Framework expects an organized unsecured group (Atlas as trustee).", "**Counter:** 5%."],
 ["A4. Warrants
§6.04(b); Ex. A
NEW", "3% struck at $1.3B TEV → 2% struck at $1.4B TEV; adds a 5-year term.", "Not disclosed in the Cover Email; Pendleton records it as unchanged. Out of the money at emergence on the base case.", "**Reject** the size and strike changes; restore 3% @ $1.3B. **Accept** the 5-year term (a helpful clarification)."],
 ["A5. MIP
§1.01; §6.05
RED", "Pool 10% → 7.5%. Vesting 50% at emergence + 50% time-based over 3 yrs → 25% at emergence + 75% performance-based over 4 yrs; metrics set by the New Board in consultation with RCL.", "Crosses all four MIP red lines (size ≥8.5%; ≥40% at emergence; not predominantly performance-based; ≤3 yrs). The Cover Email’s “up from 5%” is wrong. Leaving the metrics to a lender-controlled board is the coercion risk flagged in Framework §III.E.", "**Reject.** Restore 10% (floor 8.5%) and ≥40% vesting at emergence. Fallback: remainder 50% time / 50% performance over 3 yrs, with metrics fixed in the Plan Supplement with Company consent."],
 ["A6. Equity reconciliation
§6.06
RED (Framework §IV.A)", "Table says “Total 100%” but the Markup allocations sum to 97.5%. The Cover Email refers to a “rights offering backstop” that appears nowhere.", "A 2.5% unallocated pool is about $8.5M at base TEV and could be used later for a backstop premium to Ad Hoc members.", "**Reject.** The equity table must foot to 100%. No rights offering or backstop without a separately negotiated term sheet; any residual goes to the MIP or junior classes."],
 ["A7. Professional Fee Carveout
§1.01; §5.02; Ex. A/B
RED", "$15.0M/$7.5M → $10.0M/$5.0M. Adds that the carveout is the “sole source” of payment for fees above the DIP Budget, and that nothing above the carveout is payable without RCL and DIP Lender consent. Deletes (untracked) CD §12.03 (“not subject to reduction”; a condition to any DIP order).", "Below the $12.5M/$6.0M floors. The “sole source” language operates as an overall fee cap that conflicts with §§330/331 allowance and invites U.S. Trustee objection. It also squeezes the $1.5M committee investigation budget (DIP TS §9.3).", "**Reject.** Restore $22.5M (floor $12.5M/$6.0M), delete the “sole source” and excess-consent sentences, and restore CD §12.03."],
], widths=W, size=8)

h("B. DIP Financing", 2)
table(HD, [
 ["B1. Pricing
§5.01(b); Ex. B
RED", "SOFR + 650 → SOFR + 800; default rate SOFR + 850 → SOFR + 1,000.", "Above the SOFR + 725 maximum. Pendleton comparables put hospitality DIPs at SOFR + 450–700.", "**Counter:** SOFR + 700; hold SOFR + 725. Retain the 1.00% SOFR floor (DIP TS §3.1)."],
 ["B2. Fees
§5.01(c)–(d)
RED", "None → 3.00% upfront ($5.25M) + 2.00% exit ($3.50M).", "Total $8.75M vs. the $3M cap. The exit fee is payable on the Effective Date even when the DIP is converted into exit loans, i.e., a fee on a non-cash takeout, and it rewards a longer case.", "**Counter:** upfront fee ≤1.5% ($2.625M) and no exit fee (or an exit fee waived on conversion), combined ≤$3M. Delete the 1% commitment fee if an upfront fee is agreed."],
 ["B3. Roll-up / conversion
§5.01(e); Ex. A/B
RED", "$75M → $175M (100%) “rolled up into the Exit Facility.”", "Above the $100M cap. A full roll-up is the provision most likely to draw committee/U.S. Trustee objection; Del. Bankr. L.R. 4001-2 requires roll-ups to be highlighted and they are disfavored on an interim basis. The Markup also silently changes the concept (see Part III.C).", "**Counter:** conversion of up to $100M of DIP obligations into exit term loans at emergence; the balance repaid or refinanced at the Company’s option. No roll-up relief in the interim order. Clarify that no prepetition 1L claims are elevated."],
 ["B4. Total DIP cost
RED", "≈ $17–18M → ≈ $27–28M (est.).", "Exceeds the $22–23M ceiling; a §364 approval risk.", "Address through B1–B3; Pendleton to re-run."],
 ["B5. Budget / variance
§5.01(h); Ex. B
NEW", "Updates every 2 weeks; any adverse variance >10% is an Event of Default, with no cure. (CD RSA: ±15% line item / ±10% aggregate; DIP TS §7.1: receipts ≥85%, disbursements ≤115%, rolling 4-week test, cure in the next period.)", "A single 10% test with no cure, together with RSA termination on DIP default, is a hair trigger in a seasonal business heading into the summer peak.", "**Counter:** DIP TS §7.1 construct (85%/115%, rolling 4 weeks, professional fees and adequate protection excluded, one-period cure). Accept bi-weekly updates. Fix our own internal inconsistency."],
 ["B6. DIP Agent
Ex. B
NEW", "Briarwood (or a designee with Borrower consent) → “to be designated by the Required Consenting Lenders.”", "Removes the Company’s consent.", "**Counter:** Briarwood, or a designee reasonably acceptable to the Company."],
 ["B7. Abbreviated Exhibit B
NEW", "The Markup’s Exhibit B is a one-page table that omits key protections in the full DIP TS.", "Omitted: 2L adequate protection (DIP TS §10.2), which is needed to prime the 2L under §364(d)(1)(B) absent consent; 5-business-day remedies notice (§15.2); $1.5M investigation budget (§9.3); Disqualified Lender list (§18.2); sacred rights (§18.3); prepayment without premium (§6.3); two-draw structure (§2.3).", "**Reject.** The full March 17 DIP TS remains Exhibit B, conformed only for agreed economic changes."],
 ["B8. Interim order / DIP motion
§2.04; §4.01(b)
NEW", "Interim DIP order deadline 3 BD → 5 BD; DIP motion to be filed within 2 BD of the Petition Date.", "Gives the Company more time; the DIP motion will be a first-day filing in any event.", "**Accept.**"],
 ["B9. Adequate protection; Ad Hoc fees
Ex. B; CD §12
NEW", "The 1L adequate protection package drops the payment of Ad Hoc professional fees (CD Ex. B), and the Markup contains no counterpart to CD §12 (fees and expenses).", "Facially Company-favorable, but probably an oversight; DIP TS §§11.1(h) and 18.4 still make fees a condition to funding.", "**No action now.** Do not volunteer. Confirm the intended mechanics when papering the DIP."],
], widths=W, size=8)

h("C. Milestones and Termination", 2)
table(HD, [
 ["C1. Filing milestone
§4.01(a)
RED (at floor)", "5 BD → 3 BD after the RSA Effective Date.", "At the Framework floor. Matches the April 17 target (April 14 + 3 BD). Requires first-day papers to be final at signing.", "**Accept as a trade**, conditioned on the other milestones being restored."],
 ["C2. Case milestones
§4.01(c)–(f)
RED", "DS filing 45 → 30 days; DS approval 90 → 75; Confirmation 135 → 110; Emergence 165 → 140 (dates in Appendix A).", "Each is below the Framework floor (40/80/120/150). The 30-day DS deadline (May 17, a Saturday) is unrealistic. The Markup also drops CD §2.02’s prepetition solicitation, so the case is no longer a true prepack.", "**Counter:** open at 45/90/135/165; floor 40/80/120/150. Alternatively, if solicitation is completed prepetition, offer a combined DS/confirmation hearing in exchange for restoring the cure and extension terms."],
 ["C3. Extensions
§4.01; §4.02
NEW", "Mutual agreement → RCL “sole and absolute discretion”; adds “Time being of the essence.”", "Turns every missed milestone into an option for the lenders to terminate.", "**Reject.** Extension by the Company with RCL consent, not to be unreasonably withheld. Automatic tolling where the delay results from Court availability. Delete “time of the essence.”"],
 ["C4. Cure periods
§9.02(a),(e); §9.03(a),(e)
RED", "10 BD → 5 BD (milestone and breach cures, both directions).", "Below the 7-BD floor.", "**Counter:** 10 BD; floor 7 BD."],
 ["C5. Liquidity trigger
§1.01; §9.03(h); Ex. B
RED", "New termination right if trailing 4-week average Liquidity is below $40M, tested weekly, with no cure. Liquidity includes ABL availability.", "Above the Framework’s $30M / trailing 30-day maximum. The ABL matures **June 15, 2025** (day 59 of the case); unless it is extended or replaced, the $45M of ABL availability drops out of Liquidity mid-case and before the summer peak. It also duplicates the DIP TS §14(h) $30M covenant.", "**Reject** (DIP covenant suffices). Fallback: $30M, trailing 30-day average, counting undrawn DIP commitments and excluding the effect of ABL maturity, with a 5-BD cure."],
 ["C6. Stay relief trigger
§9.03(g)
NEW", "$25M (CD §6.02(g)) → $10M (tracked against “material value”).", "Low threshold for a 214-property portfolio, e.g., ordinary-course lift-stay motions on individual properties or insurance-backed claims.", "**Counter:** $25M; exclude stay relief for ordinary-course insured claims."],
 ["C7. Inconsistent-filing trigger
§9.03(j)
NEW", "New termination right if any Company filing is “materially inconsistent” with the RSA without RCL consent.", "Combined with “acceptable” (not “reasonably acceptable”) consent standards, this is a hair trigger.", "**Counter:** limit to filings materially inconsistent with the Term Sheet economics that are not withdrawn within 5 BD after notice."],
 ["C8. Company termination rights
§9.02(a); CD §6.01(a),(d)
NEW (untracked)", "Breach by “any Consenting Lender” → breach by the “Required Consenting Lenders.” The Company’s right to terminate if the DIP Lenders fail to fund (CD §6.01(d)) is deleted.", "A defaulting lender, or DIP lenders who refuse to fund, would leave the Company locked in. This is a serious asymmetry.", "**Reject.** Restore CD §6.01(a) and (d), and add automatic termination if the DIP is not funded within 2 BD after entry of the interim order."],
 ["C9. Governmental order
§9.02(f)
NEW", "Company may terminate on a final order prohibiting the transactions.", "Customary.", "**Accept** (make it mutual)."],
 ["C10. Effect of termination
§9.04; CD §6.04
NEW", "Garbled clause (c) (“and except for liability arising from any material breach”) expands surviving liability from willful breach to any material breach. Survival list omits fees. CD §6.04(d) vote revocation deleted.", "Drafting error with substantive effect.", "**Counter:** restore CD §6.04 (willful/intentional breach only; survival of fees, governing law and miscellaneous)."],
], widths=W, size=8)

h("D. Fiduciary Out and Alternative Transactions (Framework §III.A — hard red line)", 2)
table(HD, [
 ["D1. Notice period
§7.01(b)", "5 BD → 10 BD; notice goes to counsel.", "Crosses the ≤5 BD red line; gives the lenders a blocking window.", "**Reject.** 5 BD. Accept delivery to counsel."],
 ["D2. Disclosure
§7.01(c)", "New: notice must describe the facts, any Alternative Transaction or proposal, the **identity of the counterparty** and the material terms.", "Crosses the no-disclosure red line, chills bidders and hands the lenders competitive intelligence. CD §7(a) expressly excluded it.", "**Reject.** Restore CD §7(a) (general basis only)."],
 ["D3. Standard
§7.01(a) (untracked)", "“After consultation with outside legal counsel” → “upon the written advice of outside legal counsel.”", "Creates a documentary condition to exercising fiduciary duties and a privilege-waiver issue if the advice is later put at issue.", "**Reject.** Restore “in good faith, after consultation with outside legal counsel.”"],
 ["D4. Alternative Transaction threshold
§1.01; §7.02(a)", "“Materially better recovery to stakeholders” → a recovery to the estate at least **15% greater**. The definition says the determination is made by the RCL; §7.02(a) says the Company decides in consultation with its financial advisor.", "Crosses the no-numerical-threshold red line. At $1.3B TEV, 15% means roughly $195M of incremental value. “Recovery to the estate” is undefined, and the two provisions conflict on who decides. Delaware directors cannot contract away their fiduciary duties (*Omnicare, Inc. v. NCS Healthcare, Inc.*, 818 A.2d 914 (Del. 2003); *Paramount Commc’ns Inc. v. QVC Network Inc.*, 637 A.2d 34 (Del. 1994)), and bankruptcy courts scrutinize lock-ups without workable outs (*cf. In re Innkeepers USA Trust*, 442 B.R. 227 (Bankr. S.D.N.Y. 2010)).", "**Reject.** Restore “materially better,” as determined by the Board in good faith after consultation with Pendleton and counsel, taking into account certainty, timing and conditionality."],
 ["D5. Matching right
§7.02(b) (partly untracked)", "10 BD → 15 BD; adds information parity (including non-public information given to the counterparty) and a ban on exclusivity with the counterparty. The Board’s determination that a match is “comparable or better” (CD §7(b)(iv)) is deleted, so the RCL decide for themselves whether they have matched.", "Each element crosses a red line or removes Board control.", "**Reject.** 10 BD; the Board determines whether the match is comparable; no information parity. Confirm that no break-up fee is sought (none appears)."],
], widths=W, size=8)
EOF
echo ok'

CD §6.04(d) vote revocation deleted.", "Drafting error with substantive effect.", "**Counter:** restore CD §6.04 (willful/intentional breach only; survival of fees, governing law and miscellaneous)."],
], widths=W, size=8)

h("D. Fiduciary Out and Alternative Transactions (Framework §III.A — hard red line)", 2)
table(HD, [
 ["D1. Notice period
§7.01(b)", "5 BD → 10 BD; notice goes to counsel.", "Crosses the ≤5 BD red line; gives the lenders a blocking window.", "**Reject.** 5 BD. Accept delivery to counsel."],
 ["D2. Disclosure
§7.01(c)", "New: notice must describe the facts, any Alternative Transaction or proposal, the **identity of the counterparty** and the material terms.", "Crosses the no-disclosure red line, chills bidders and hands the lenders competitive intelligence. CD §7(a) expressly excluded it.", "**Reject.** Restore CD §7(a) (general basis only)."],
 ["D3. Standard
§7.01(a) (untracked)", "“After consultation with outside legal counsel” → “upon the written advice of outside legal counsel.”", "Creates a documentary condition to exercising fiduciary duties and a privilege-waiver issue if the advice is later put at issue.", "**Reject.** Restore “in good faith, after consultation with outside legal counsel.”"],
 ["D4. Alternative Transaction threshold
§1.01; §7.02(a)", "“Materially better recovery to stakeholders” → a recovery to the estate at least **15% greater**. The definition says the determination is made by the RCL; §7.02(a) says the Company decides in consultation with its financial advisor.", "Crosses the no-numerical-threshold red line. At $1.3B TEV, 15% means roughly $195M of incremental value. “Recovery to the estate” is undefined, and the two provisions conflict on who decides. Delaware directors cannot contract away their fiduciary duties (*Omnicare, Inc. v. NCS Healthcare, Inc.*, 818 A.2d 914 (Del. 2003); *Paramount Commc’ns Inc. v. QVC Network Inc.*, 637 A.2d 34 (Del. 1994)), and bankruptcy courts scrutinize lock-ups without workable outs (*cf. In re Innkeepers USA Trust*, 442 B.R. 227 (Bankr. S.D.N.Y. 2010)).", "**Reject.** Restore “materially better,” as determined by the Board in good faith after consultation with Pendleton and counsel, taking into account certainty, timing and conditionality."],
 ["D5. Matching right
§7.02(b) (partly untracked)", "10 BD → 15 BD; adds information parity (including non-public information given to the counterparty) and a ban on exclusivity with the counterparty. The Board’s determination that a match is “comparable or better” (CD §7(b)(iv)) is deleted, so the RCL decide for themselves whether they have matched.", "Each element crosses a red line or removes Board control.", "**Reject.** 10 BD; the Board determines whether the match is comparable; no information parity. Confirm that no break-up fee is sought (none appears)."],
], widths=W, size=8)
EOF
echo ok'

table(HD, [
 ["E1. Pre-petition Board Observers\n§3.01(h); §11.02\nRED", "New: two RCL-designated observers from the RSA Effective Date to the Petition Date, with 2 BD notice of every board/committee meeting, contemporaneous board materials and attendance rights. A\nFLEX", "“Determined by the Company in consultation with RCL” (CD §11.01) → 7 members: 4 lender designees, 1 2L designee, the CEO, and 1 independent mutually agreed.", "Within Framework §IV.C flexibility (lender majority, management seat, 1–2 independents).", "**Accept with modifications:** a second independent (e.g., 4 lender + 2 independent + CEO, with the 2L seat drawn from the independents if the 2L class accepts); an independent audit committee; designations by the Plan Supplement deadline."],
 ["E3. Management continuity\nCD §11.02 (deleted, untracked)", "Deletes the covenant that current officers continue through the Effective Date and receive good-faith new employment agreements.", "Retention risk, compounded by A5.", "**Reject.** Restore CD §11.02."],
 ["E4. Efforts / consent standards\n§§1.01, 2.02, 2.03, 3.01(a),(c),(e)\nNEW (partly untracked)", "“Commercially reasonable efforts” → “reasonable best efforts and in consultation with RCL.” Plan, DS, Confirmation Order and DIP Credit Agreement must be “acceptable” (not “reasonably acceptable”) to RCL.  ["E5. Exclusivity\n§3.01(g)\nNEW", "Company must support “any motion by the RCL” to extend exclusivity under §1121.", "Exclusivity belongs to the debtor; probably a drafting error, but it could be read to let the lenders steer exclusivity.", "**Counter:** the Company will seek extensions and the lenders will support them."],
 ["E6. Information\n§3.01(f)\nNEW", "Adds weekly cash flow projections and variance reports.", "Already required under DIP TS §7.2.", "**Accept.**"],
], widths=W, size=8)

h("F. Releases and Injunction", 2)
table(HD, [
 ["F1. Third-party releases\n§10.02; §10.03; §13.10; Ex. A\nNEW (Framework §V.D)", "New: holders that vote to accept, are deemed to accept, **abstain**, or vote to reject without opting out are deemed to release the Released Parties from all claims related to the Debtors. Del. 2024) have declined to treat silence or a failure to return an opt-out as consent in some settings, and the U.S. Trustee objects routinely. Binding abstainers, deemed acceptors (ABL, general unsecured creditors) and holders of cancelled equity is unlikely to survive. Combined with C2–C4, a release dispute at confirmation becomes a lender termination right. The Cover Email’s claim that the releases bind “non-consenting parties” as “standard” Delaware practice is inconsistent with *Purdue*.", "**Counter:** consensual releases only. Releasing parties are holders in voting classes that vote to accept (and do not opt out) or affirmatively opt in, with conspicuous ballot disclosure; no deemed consent for non-voting, deemed-rejecting or unimpaired holders unless they opt in. Company D&Os and professionals to be Released Parties. Consult the appellate group per Framework §V.D, and verify current Delaware authority before the turn."],
 ["F2. Carve-outs and limits\nCD §§9.02–9.04 (deleted, untracked)", "Deletes the exclusion for fraud, willful misconduct and gross negligence; the statement that non-parties are not bound; and the “Plan releases no broader than RSA” covenant.", "Carve-outs are standard in Delaware; their absence will draw objection.", "**Reject.** Restore CD §§9.03–9.04."],
 ["F3. Mutual release scope\n§10.01\nNEW", "General release → claims “relating to or arising under the First Lien Credit Agreement, this Agreement, or the Restructuring Transactions.”", "Narrows both directions. The estate’s release of the lenders shrinks (estate-favorable); the lenders’ release of the D&Os also shrinks.", "**Accept the narrower estate release**, provided the lenders’ release of the Company Parties and D&Os is not narrower. Estate release of lenders subject to an independent director review and the committee challenge period."],
], widths=W, size=8)

h("G. Lock-Up and Transfers", 2)
table(HD, [
 ["G1. Permitted Transfers\n§8.01(c); §1.01 (QT)\nRED", "New: each lender may transfer 15% of its claims to non-parties without a joinder (aggregate cap 15%).", "Framework: transfers without joinder must not be permitted. Locked support could fall to about 53.0% of the class (Part III.F).", "**Reject.**"],
 ["G2. Joinder window\n§8.01(a); Ex. D\nFLEX", "5 BD → 10 BD.", "Above the 7-BD limit.", "**Counter:** 7 BD (the Framework flex)."],
 ["G3.  ["G4. Lender support covenants\nCD §3.02(f),(h),(i) (deleted, untracked); §3.02(g)", "Deletes the no-enforcement/forbearance covenant, the good-faith negotiation of definitive documents, and support for first-day motions. The no-alternative-plan covenant is qualified to “inconsistent with the Restructuring Transactions.”", "Together with G5, the lenders’ obligations become largely illusory.", "**Reject.** Restore CD §3.02(f), (h) and (i)."],
 ["G5. Recital E adds “or liquidation.”", "The most dangerous structural change.  ["G6. RSA Effective Date\n§1.01\nNEW", "Execution “by each of the Parties” (CD: execution by holders of at least $742.6M, i.e., all nine).", "Any single holdout blocks effectiveness. The Company also needs about $50.7M of additional 1L support.", "**Counter:** effectiveness on execution by holders of at least 60% of 1L claims; the Company to solicit additional 1L signatories."],
], widths=W, size=8)

h("H. Operating Controls", 2)
table(HD, [
 ["H1. Cash Collateral\n§2.05; Ex. B\nRED (Framework §V.C)", "New: RCL consent for use of cash collateral outside the ordinary course above $2M per transaction or $5M in aggregate; 3-BD response; no deemed consent; overrides any court order.", "Far below the $10M/$25M Framework minimum. Hotel capex, seasonal staffing and franchise payments routinely exceed $2M. Purporting to override Court orders also invites U.S. Trustee objection as a delegation of debtor-in-possession authority.", "**Counter:** $10M per transaction / $25M aggregate; budgeted items and payments under first-day orders excluded; deemed consent if no response within 3 BD; delete “notwithstanding any order.”"],
], widths=W, size=8)

h("I. Representations and Warranties", 2)
table(HD, [
 ["I1. Financial information\n§12.01(d) (untracked)", "Knowledge-qualified and materiality-qualified rep (CD §10.01(e)) → flat “accurate and complete”; references audited FY2024 statements prepared by Hartfield & Dunn.", "A flat rep, brought down at the RSA Effective Date, creates a termination right (§9.03(a)).  ["I3.  ["I4. Lender reps\n§12.02(b)\nNEW", "Adds a rep that holdings are not subject to other voting agreements.", "Helpful.", "**Accept.** Restore the QIB/AI rep (G3)."],

h("K. Conforming and Clarifying Changes (Accept)", 2)
para("We recommend accepting the following without discussion: “or any successor thereto” agent references; “as amended, restated, supplemented, or otherwise modified” formulations; “which” to “that”; the “Bankruptcy Code” typo fix; deletion of the duplicate “Company Parties” definition in Recital A; the no-admission sentence in Recital D; the Termination Date cross-reference fix; email notice (§13.01(d)) and the Clearbridge copy; the entire-agreement supersession language (§13.05); electronic signatures (§13.08); the governing-law reference to the Bankruptcy Code (§13.02); “including, without limitation” in “Reorganized Company”; Joinder effectiveness on delivery (§8.02) and notice address (Ex. S=/home/user/Lawless_Research_Lab/harvey_lab/sbx.sh; R=/home/user/Lawless_Research_Lab/harvey_lab/vendor/harvey-labs/results/bankruptcy-restructuring/analyze-counterparty-markup-of-restructuring-support-agreement/claude-code-session/20261016-040607; $S $R 'cat > /workspace/gen/p7.py <<"EOF"
def scen(tl, conv, fees, carve, e1, e2, e3, mip, full=False):
    ded = tl + (175.0 if full else conv) + 80 + fees + carve + 25
    eq = 1300 - ded
    return eq, tl + e1*eq, e2*eq, e3*eq, mip*eq
rows = []
for label, args in [("Company Draft", (595, 75, 0, 22.5, .72, .12, .06, .10)),
                    ("Ad Hoc Markup", (655, 175, 8.75, 15, .78, .08, .04, .075)),
                    ("Company counter (opening, carveout $22.5M)", (625, 100, 1.75, 22.5, .75, .10, .05, .10))]:
    a = scen(*args); b = scen(*args, full=True)
    rows.append([label, "$%.1f / $%.1f" % (a[0], b[0]), "$%.1f (%.1f%%) / $%.1f (%.1f%%)" % (a[1], a[1]/11.9, b[1], b[1]/11.9),
                 "$%.1f (%.1f%%) / $%.1f (%.1f%%)" % (a[2], a[2]/3.8, b[2], b[2]/3.8), "$%.1f (%.1f%%) / $%.1f (%.1f%%)" % (a[3], a[3]/3.0, b[3], b[3]/3.0)])
h("B. Indicative economics of the counter (TEV $1.3B)", 2)
para("Each cell shows the Pendleton methodology first (deducting only the rolled/converted DIP amount) and then our like-for-like view (deducting the full $175M DIP takeout in every case). The counter assumes S+700 on the DIP and a 1.0% upfront fee ($1.75M). These are indicative figures for Pendleton to confirm.", align="justify")
table(["Scenario", "Equity value", "1L total", "2L", "Unsecured (excl. warrants)"], rows, widths=[1.6, 1.0, 1.4, 1.3, 1.2], size=8)
para("On Pendleton’s methodology the counter delivers a **higher total 1L class recovery than the Markup** (about $958.7M vs. $921.2M), because it moves value back from DIP-only economics to the class. That gives us a strong argument with the Ad Hoc Group’s non-DIP members and with the 37.6% of 1L holders outside the group. On the like-for-like view, the counter still gives the 1L class more than the Company Draft did, while restoring junior recoveries to levels the Framework regards as consensual.", align="justify")

h("C. Junior creditor engagement", 2)
para("We recommend that the Company not accept the Ad Hoc Group’s request to defer all junior engagement until solicitation. The Framework contemplated engagement once the first lien framework is substantially agreed, and that point should come **before** RSA execution, for five reasons. (1) The DIP primes the 2L liens, so the Company needs either 2L consent, a deemed consent under the August 12, 2019 intercreditor agreement (to be reviewed), or adequate protection that satisfies §364(d)(1)(B). (2) The 2L and unsecured classes are voting classes in a prepack, and a rejection forces a §1129(b) cramdown and valuation contest that the milestones cannot accommodate. (3) Their trading levels (28 and 8 cents) signal they will fight. (4) The releases, the carveout and the roll-up are the provisions they are most likely to attack. (5) The Board must be able to show it considered all stakeholders. We suggest a confidential outreach to Kelton Harris & Roe under an NDA once terms with the Ad Hoc Group are agreed in principle (target the week of April 7), with a joinder path for the 2L in the RSA.", align="justify")

h("D. Process and timetable (RSA target April 14; Petition Date April 17)", 2)
for t in [
 "**April 3–4:** Send the process note to Mr. Garvey (reservation of rights; request for a true comparison against the March 17 draft; the clarification list in Part VII). Ask Pendleton to re-run the Schedule (DIP takeout, warrants, counter package, DIP all-in cost, leverage, a weekly liquidity forecast through ABL maturity and the summer peak against the $40M/$30M tests).",
 "**By April 7:** Board briefing through Ms. Pratt and Ms. Holloway on the red-line items (fiduciary out, DIP, carveout, milestones, MIP, observers, releases). Consult the appellate group on releases (Framework §V.D). Deliver the issues list to Sternwick ahead of the April 7–8 call with Clearbridge and Pendleton.",
 "**April 8–9:** Circulate the Company turn (redline against the March 17 draft), with the full DIP TS restored as Exhibit B and conformed.",
 "**April 9–14:** Negotiate; first-day papers final by April 14 so the 3-BD filing milestone can be met; parallel discussions with Briarwood on ABL maturity and a postpetition ABL; outreach to Kelton Harris & Roe.",
 "All communications go through Ms. Vasquez (Framework §VI.4). No signaling of flexibility before the Board briefing."]:
    bullet(t)

h("VII. Clarifications to Request from Sternwick & Calloway")
for t in [
 "What is the “rights offering backstop” referenced in the Cover Email, and how is the 2.5% of unallocated equity intended to be used?",
 "Was the warrant change (2% @ $1.4B) intended? It is not described in the Cover Email.",
 "Roll-up mechanics: does the Markup contemplate any elevation of prepetition 1L claims into the DIP, or only conversion of DIP loans into exit loans? How is the exit fee treated on conversion?",
 "Observer rights: do they terminate on the Petition Date (§11.02) or at emergence (Cover Email)?",
 "Why was Schedule 1 reduced to four entities, and was the deletion of CD §§3.02(f), 6.01(d), 8.05(b), 9.03 and 11.02 intended?",
 "Which credit agreement and indenture dates do the Ad Hoc Group’s records reflect, and which entity (Hollcroft or Redstone) will sign?",
 "Exit term loan terms (pricing, maturity, amortization, covenants) and the proposed DIP participation mechanics for 1L holders outside the Ad Hoc Group.",
 "Under §7.02(a) and the definition of “Alternative Transaction,” who determines the 15% threshold, and how is “recovery to the estate” measured?"]:
    num(t)

h("Appendix A — Milestone Calendar (assumes RSA Effective Date Monday, April 14, 2025, and Petition Date Thursday, April 17, 2025)")
table(["Milestone", "Company Draft", "Markup", "Framework floor"], [
 ["Chapter 11 filing", "5 BD → Mon. Apr. 21", "3 BD → Thu. Apr. 17", "3 BD → Apr. 17"],
 ["DIP motion filed", "—", "2 BD → Mon. Apr. 21", "—"],
 ["Interim DIP order", "3 BD → Tue. Apr. 22", "5 BD → Thu. Apr. 24", "—"],
 ["Final DIP order", "45 days → Sun. Jun. 1", "45 days → Sun. Jun. 1", "—"],
 ["DS and Plan filed", "45 days → Sun. Jun. 1", "30 days → Sat. May 17", "40 days → Tue. May 27"],
 ["DS approved", "90 days → Wed. Jul. 16", "75 days → Tue. Jul. 1", "80 days → Sun. Jul. 6"],
 ["Confirmation Order", "135 days → Sat. Aug. 30", "110 days → Tue. Aug. 5", "120 days → Fri. Aug. 15"],
 ["Effective Date", "165 days → Mon. Sep. 29", "140 days → Thu. Sep. 4", "150 days → Sun. Sep. 14"],
 ["Reference: ABL maturity", "Sun. Jun. 15, 2025 (day 59)", "same", "—"],
 ["Reference: DIP maturity (6 months)", "Fri. Oct. 17, 2025", "same", "—"],
], widths=[1.7, 1.6, 1.6, 1.6], size=8.5)
para("Several deadlines fall on weekends. The turn should provide that a milestone falling on a non-Business Day rolls to the next Business Day.", italic=True, size=9)
EOF
echo ok'
